# `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's non-initialised `.worklog` (and can build `.worklog/.worklog`)

> **Provenance:** `discovered-from:SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (which was transferred
> from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT`, itself `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`).
> Filed separately by producer decision so the parent fix stays narrow.

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/code_freeze.py` carries its **own** copy of
`_detect_worklog_dir()`. It builds ancestor candidates as `parent / ".worklog"`
for every parent and accepts any `.worklog` directory without checking that it
is initialised. Consequences:

- from a linked worktree root whose committed `.worklog/` holds only
  `config.yaml`, `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
  `<worktree>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` — a marker file that can never exist,
  so the fail-closed freeze gate silently sees "no freeze";
- from `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` (no committed `.worklog`), a
  stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory would be selected, giving
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

The correct marker in both cases is `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

## Users

- **AI agent running `/skill:implement` from a worktree** — the implement
  workflow consults the code-freeze marker; reading the wrong path makes the
  freeze gate miss an active freeze.
  Story: *As an implementing agent in a worktree, an active code freeze must be
  detected, so I stop instead of landing a commit that the freeze forbids.*
- **Producer/operator** — an activated freeze must be effective immediately for
  every checkout.
  Story: *As the producer, when I activate a freeze, agents working in
  worktrees must observe it without extra `--worklog-dir` instructions.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs one resolution rule, not two divergent copies.
  Story: *As a maintainer, code-freeze marker resolution must not silently drift
  from `status_lifecycle`'s worklog-dir rule.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves the main marker.** With cwd at a linked
      worktree root that has a committed, **uninitialised** `.worklog/`
      (`config.yaml` only), `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.
- [ ] **AC2 — no `.worklog/.worklog` nesting.** With cwd inside
      `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`, the marker path is
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` even when a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC3 — explicit `project_root` unchanged.** `code_freeze_marker_path(<root>)`
      still returns `<root>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` and is unaffected by the
      cwd-based rule.
- [ ] **AC4 — one rule, not two.** `code_freeze._detect_worklog_dir()` either
      re-uses the shared resolution helper from `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
      (preferred — no duplicated walk) or mirrors it exactly, with a comment
      naming the shared rule as authoritative.
- [ ] **AC5 — unit tests.** Hermetic `tmp_path` tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` for AC1–AC3 (no real
      `git worktree`, no network), alongside the existing marker tests.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The `code_freeze.py` docstrings state the
      initialised-only / no-nesting rule; if resolution is shared, note it in
      `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` next to the `StatusLifecycle` note.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not widen the freeze semantics: this is a path-resolution fix, not a
  change to how a freeze is activated, cleared, or enforced.
- Keep the existing public API (`code_freeze_marker_path`, marker read/write
  helpers) and their `project_root` behaviour unchanged.
- Prefer re-using the shared helper over a second walk; if that would create a
  circular import, mirror the rule and reference the canonical one in a
  comment.
- Gate order: build → test → commit; no ad-hoc `pytest` — run tests through the
  test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake of the parent item)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 48) order:
  explicit `project_root` → `<cwd>/.worklog` → `<git toplevel>/.worklog` →
  `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`, each gated on `is_dir()` only.
- `code_freeze_marker_path()` (~line 90) uses that helper and falls back to
  `<cwd>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` when nothing resolves.
- The same candidate-construction defect is proven in
  `status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` (parent item
  `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB`, AC1–AC3) — this item is the same rule applied to the
  code-freeze copy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` / marker path
  resolution (~lines 48–101).
- `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` — new worktree-layout cases
  (AC1–AC3).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — one sentence alongside the
  `StatusLifecycle` resolution note (if the rule is shared).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the shared helper is exported
  for reuse (no behaviour change expected here).

## Related work

- `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` — parent fix for `status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()`
  / `worklog_dir_flag()` (same rule, `wl`-facing seam). This item should land
  after it so the shared rule exists.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`, `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine) —
  discovery chain for the original defect.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: freeze bypass stays latent** until this item is implemented, if the
  parent fix lands alone. Mitigation: the parent item's docs state the
  code-freeze copy is still defective and link here.
- **Risk: duplicated rule drifts again.** Mitigation: AC4 prefers the shared
  helper.
- **Scope-creep risk:** touching freeze activation/enforcement or adding new
  marker features — out of scope; record such ideas as separate items.
- **Assumption:** the implement workflow's freeze check is the only consumer of
  `code_freeze_marker_path()`; verified by grep during implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Fold this into the parent `worklog_dir_flag` fix?**
  **Answer (producer):** *"file separately"* — filed here; the parent item stays
  narrow. Source: operator reply in the intake session
  `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`, relayed via
  `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (Appendix Q2).

Cross-repo: TCE CG-0MW2151GL003SV5E (originating item), ContextHub WL-0MW2A3NAP0088IE9 (template change).

## Why

The implement skill's dev-push block documents the gate as bound to the pushed
commit (`run_tests.py --gate-commit <sha> --project-root <root>`) and as
mirroring the cache from the checkout actually gated. After the canonical
template gained `mirror_suite_cache` (SA-0MW20Y5YI004QS3M) the remaining gap is
the commit binding: `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` still runs the suite unbound. Once
WL-0MW2A3NAP0088IE9 lands, the template delivers the documented contract and
the skill text must describe the final behaviour — including the refusal
semantics and the dirty-checkout impact — as canonical-template behaviour, not
as a repository-local patch.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (step 9 dev-push block) states that the
   commit-bound gate (`--gate-commit` + `--project-root`, multi-commit refusal,
   cache mirrored from the gate-resolved root) is canonical-template behaviour
   delivered by `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT`, and that `.githooks/pre-push` must not
   be patched locally.
2. The refusal semantics are stated: when no clean checkout holds the pushed
   commit the push is refused (exit 2) with the `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` escape
   hatch; `.gitignore`d `.worklog/` churn does not make a checkout dirty.
3. The text names the runner-compatibility behaviour chosen in the template
   (Q1 = (c): an explicit pre-check refusal when the resolved runner predates
   `--gate-commit`, instead of an argparse error).
4. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (docs-only change;
   the docs lint/graph checks and the dev-push gate are the enforcement).

## Constraints

- Prose-only change in the implement skill; no behaviour change in this repo.
- Do not restate the template's shell code; describe the contract.
- Sequence after WL-0MW2A3NAP0088IE9 so the documentation matches delivered
  behaviour.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — dev-push gate block (the `--gate-commit`
  note and the mirroring note).

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-17)

### Dependency

- **Depends on `WL-0MW2A3NAP0088IE9`** (ContextHub — pre-push hook template
  commit binding). Recorded as a `wl dep` edge (foreign, resolved); the
  constraint "sequence after it so the documentation matches delivered
  behaviour" is satisfied formally by that edge. See the pre-implementation
  verification below before relying on it in substance.

### Pre-implementation verification (correctness gate for AC1/AC3)

Before describing the gate as *delivered* template behaviour, re-check the
template:

```bash
grep -n 'gate-commit' ../ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts
```

**Observed 2026-11-17 (ContextHub dev/main, v1.0.30): no match.** The embedded
template still runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env
--project-root "$repo_root"` and only *warns* when the checked-out `HEAD` is
not the pushed ref; the `--gate-commit` block added by `WL-0MW2A3NAP0088IE9`
(commit `12138e0e`) was removed by revert `df878ed3`
(`WL-0MW2N56M2004PSRP`) and the producer decision recorded on
`WL-0MW2A3NAP0088IE9` ("the commit-bound gate is canonical … the revert must
be re-applied") has not landed, although that item is closed
"Shipped in v1.0.29". SorraAgents' committed `.githooks/pre-push` **does**
implement the full contract.

Rule for implementation:

- Template **lacks** the block → document the contract and its refusal
  semantics (as AC1–AC3 require) attributed to the template version that
  delivers it, and say plainly that a repo whose canonical hook has no
  `--gate-commit` block still only warns. Never claim delivered behaviour the
  template lacks.
- Template **has** the block → document it directly as canonical-template
  behaviour.

### Resolved decisions (producer, 2026-11-17)

- **Q1 — dependency:** make this item dependent on `WL-0MW2A3NAP0088IE9`. Done
  (`wl dep list SA-0MW2A3WWQ008TDZV`).
- **Q2 — where the CG items live:** producer pointed at `../ContextHub`; in
  practice `CG-0MW2151GL003SV5E` resolves from
  `Tableau-Card-Engine`'s store (ContextHub returns *not found*). Read
  read-only for AC wording; no cross-repo write.
- **Q3 — "multi-commit refusal":** the wording in AC1 is this item's own; the

  sha) are not treated as gated commits. Exit-code note for the docs: the
  hook's multi-commit refusal exits **1**; the runner's "no clean checkout
  holds the pushed commit" refusal exits **2** with `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`.

### Scope and approach

Single prose edit in the **step 9 dev-push block** of
`skill/implement/SKILL.md`. No child work items: docs-only, one Key File, four
ACs, one section — decomposition would add dispatch overhead without a

- Rewrite/extend the existing "Pushing from a worktree" note into a

4. **AC4 — enforcement:** docs-lint/graph checks and the dev-push gate; no
   behaviour change, so the change rides the normal changed-scope finish gate
   plus the dev-push full suite.

### Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** What is Q1 = (c) (runner compatibility)? **A (producer):** CG work

## Goal

Decide and implement how non-interactive (herdr-downtime-dispatched) audits avoid the in-main-slot pending-screens trap: a dispatched audit has no interactive invoking session to perform the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens, so by construction every dispatched parent audit lands in the unserviced state.

Discovered-from: SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (audit comment 2026-10-29, "Adjacent scope note 1"). Distinct from the D1/D2 resume defects: even with a working resume cycle, nobody services a dispatched audit's screens.

## Context and Discovery

This item was auto-dispatched by the herdr-downtime worker on 2026-11-17. The root cause is that the in-main-slot mode (introduced in SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE) relies on an interactive agent session to parse and execute `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` markers emitted by the audit runner. When a downtime-dispatched audit runs non-interactively, there is no session to consume these markers, so child screens are effectively lost — the audit hangs in an unserviceable pending state.

## Producer decision (AC1) — runner-side context detection

**Decision (producer, 2026-11-17):** Adopt the **runner-side** approach. The audit runner resolves `child_in_main_slot=False` when it detects it is running in a dispatched / non-interactive context, so child screens execute in isolated `pi` subprocesses with the runner's own parsing and retry — no interactive session required.

**Rejected alternative:** dispatcher-side `--no-child-in-main-slot` flag passed from the herdr downtime worker. Rejected because it only covers one caller: any other non-interactive entry point (cron, CI, future dispatchers) would still emit unserviceable screens. Runner-side detection makes the behaviour a property of the runner, not of each caller.

**Accepted trade-off:** separate-process child audits cost one `pi` subprocess per child (more expensive than in-main-slot), but they need no interactive session and therefore always make progress — strictly better than hanging in the unserviced pending state.

**Resolution precedence (AC4):** explicit `--child-in-main-slot` / `--no-child-in-main-slot` flag > `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` env var > dispatch/non-interactive detection > default `True`. The explicit flag and env var keep their existing absolute precedence, so an operator can always override detection.

**Resolution source must be logged** (e.g. `child_in_main_slot resolved to False (source: dispatch-detection)`) so the chosen mode is traceable in runner output and audit logs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. AC1: The chosen mechanism (runner-side dispatch detection) and the rejected alternative (dispatcher-side flag) are recorded on this item with the rationale and the accepted trade-off — already satisfied by the `## Producer decision (AC1)` section above; the implementation must honour it.
2. AC2: Dispatched audits no longer emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens that nobody services: a dispatched run either completes its child screens itself in isolated `pi` subprocesses or reports a documented, actionable state.
3. AC3: An interactive audit launched from an agent session keeps in-main-slot mode by default — no behaviour change for the interactive path.
4. AC4: Regression coverage proves the resolution precedence (explicit flag > env `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` > dispatch detection > default `true`), with `wl`/`pi` mocked (no real subprocess).
5. AC5: The resolved mode and its source are logged, and the log line is asserted in the regression coverage.

## Implementation notes (runner-side)

- Add a dispatch/non-interactive detector (e.g. an explicit dispatch marker env such as a herdr/downtime-dispatched indicator) consulted inside `_resolve_child_in_main_slot()` after the CLI flag and `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` env var.
- Return the resolution source alongside the boolean so the caller can log it; keep the helper backward-compatible for existing callers (or add a sibling helper returning `(value, source)`).
- Emit one clear log line at resolution time naming the source; on the dispatched path the runner must not emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]`.
- Ensure the downtime worker sets the dispatch marker (or the runner can otherwise identify a non-interactive context) — confirm the marker's origin during implementation and record it in a comment.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_child_in_main_slot`, `cmd_issue` child-mode resolution, logging of the resolution source
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — `TestChildInMainSlotGateResolution` (extend with dispatch-detection precedence cases)
- herdr downtime worker dispatch path — must set the dispatch marker; locate before editing

## Dependencies

- Related to SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (its resume fixes are a prerequisite for any in-main-slot dispatch to be recoverable, but this item is not blocked by it).
- Related to SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS (Sweep stale in-main-slot pending-screens signals) — adjacent scope.

## Deliverables

- Runner-side dispatch detection with logged resolution source + regression tests.

## Impact

Downtime-dispatched audits now finish their own child screens instead of stalling in a pending state that nobody services, so overnight audit runs produce verdicts without human intervention.

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- **Q:** Which mechanism should be adopted — dispatcher-side `--no-child-in-main-slot` flag, or runner-side dispatch/context detection? — **Answer (producer):** Option 2, runner-side context detection. Source: interactive reply on 2026-11-17 ("2"). Rationale recorded above: covers every non-interactive entry point, not just the herdr downtime worker. No further questions; no prior answer changed.

- **Q:** Which env var should the herdr downtime worker set for dispatch detection — a new `HERDR_DOWNTIME=1` marker (recommended) or the existing `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT=false`? — **Answer (producer):** Option 1, `HERDR_DOWNTIME=1`. Source: interactive reply on 2026-11-17 ("Option 1"). Rationale: it keeps the detection tier meaningful (source `dispatch-detection` stays reachable and assertable, as AC5 requires), keeps the caller declaring *context* while the runner decides *mode*, and does not overload the documented operator-override env var with a third meaning. Reusing `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT=false` would collapse the dispatch tier into the `env` tier and re-create the rejected dispatcher-side coupling one layer down. Prior recommendation in the same session: `HERDR_DOWNTIME=1` (unchanged; no answer revised). Watch item recorded: the marker is emitted from ContentCreator's herdr dispatch path, which cannot be edited from this repository's worktree — tracked as child SA-0MWL51XNM001HMVC (cross-repo hand-off).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MU32TE120012T49** – R5: Enforce the child-audit execution contract (no silent pending child screens) (completed)
- **SA-0MVAWFQ4A002XCAO** – Interactive audit regression guard (completed)
- **SA-0MVAWFPVU001E1T0** – Unserviced in-main-slot verdict tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mt2xrgeu0009qre, 0mvstz71j001p67s, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+147 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+146 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+146 more)

# `scripts/install_pi.sh` wires git hooks but never refreshes the globally resolved `wl`, so a stale `dist` can silently revert the canonical hook template

discovered-from:CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU (Tableau-Card-Engine — "Restore pre-push test-cache mirroring in the canonical wl hook template", AC2 tail clause: recorded as a follow-up, not fixed there)

## Problem statement

`scripts/install_pi.sh` installs and *wires* the project's git hooks
(`.githooks/*` copies + `core.hooksPath`), but it never refreshes the `wl` binary
those hooks depend on. On this framework, `wl` is not installed from a registry
— it is **npm-linked to the `ContextHub` checkout**, and `ContextHub/dist` is
gitignored. So the template that `wl init` / `wl doctor upgrade` emits is
whatever was last built into a *local, uncommitted* `dist`, which can predate (or
diverging from) the committed hook. The next `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` then
silently rewrites a consuming repository's `.githooks/pre-push` from that stale
template and deletes capabilities the repo legitimately carries.

The concrete incident class: `mirror_suite_cache` (the dev-push gate's
test-cache mirroring, `CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU` / ContextHub `WL-0MW20XXWE00466FP`)
existed only in a stale `ContextHub/dist` build for a while. A rebuild of the
linked `wl` from a `dev` that lacked the template change, followed by
`wl doctor upgrade --confirm`, removes the capability from every consuming
repo, with exit 0 and no warning — the invariant "a worktree-originated `dev`
push leaves a green cached full-suite entry the main checkout can read" then
breaks silently.

## Verified facts (checked 2026-11-04 on this host)

1. **`wl` is npm-linked, not registry-installed.**
   - `npm ls -g --depth=0` → `worklog@1.0.27 -> ./../../../home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`
   - `/usr/local/bin/wl` → `../lib/node_modules/worklog/dist/cli.js`, which
     `readlink -f` resolves to `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/dist/cli.js`.
   - The package version stays `1.0.27` across template changes, so the version
     number alone cannot tell you whether the *template* is current.
2. **The template lives only in the built `dist`.** `ContextHub/.gitignore`
   line 86 ignores `dist`; `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` is compiled from
   `ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` into
   `ContextHub/dist/doctor/hook-upgrade.js`, so the `wl` a machine runs is
   whatever branch/dirty state was last built there.
3. **The installer wires hooks but never touches `wl`.** The hook block is
   `scripts/install_pi.sh:317-412` (comment header at :317): step 1 copies
   `$SRC_DIR/.githooks/pre-push` (v3) or `pre-push.v2` into the project's
   `.githooks/` only when absent (:347-361), step 2 sets
   `core.hooksPath = .githooks` (:363-370), then it verifies the global
   context-audit skill (:373-380), per-project thresholds (:383-388) and the git
   identity (:390-408). There is **no** `npm run build`, `npm link`, `npm i -g`
   or version check anywhere in the installer.
4. **The destructive step is `wl doctor upgrade`, not the installer.**
   `ContextHub/src/commands/doctor/upgrade.ts:98` emits the upgrade set and
   `upgradeHooks()` (`ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts:603-643`) writes
   every `outdated` hook with `fs.writeFileSync(hookPath,
   h.committedContent, { mode: 0o755 })` — a **whole-file overwrite** of the
   repo's committed hook with the template baked into the running `wl`, i.e. the
   stale `dist`. The result is reported as success ("Upgraded from
   .githooks/").
5. **Why it matters (consuming repos).** Every repository in the framework uses
   `core.hooksPath = .githooks`, so the hook file *is* the gate. After a stale
   rebuild + upgrade, `.githooks/pre-push` no longer mirrors the gate run's
   cache entries into the main checkout's `.worklog/cache`, and
   `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` reports `missing` at the just-
   pushed commit (and audit F3 loses its cached green evidence).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fail loudly on template skew.** The installer (and/or the hook-wiring
  step it owns) fails loudly — non-zero exit or an explicit, actionable
  `WARNING` naming both sides — when the template baked into the resolved `wl`
  predates/differs from the hook the repository commits, instead of leaving the
  operator with a `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` that deletes the divergence.
  *Verification:* a new test case drives the installer with a sandboxed `HOME`
  and a stub `wl` whose template lacks a marker present in the repo's committed
  hook, and asserts the refusal/warning text; the up-to-date case stays silent.
- **AC2 — Regression test in the existing installer suite.**
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` gains the skew cases next to the
  existing hook-wiring cases, with a sandboxed `HOME` (no live `~/.pi`, no live
  npm global root) so the test is hermetic and CI-safe.
  *Verification:* the new cases fail against today's installer and pass after
  the change.
- **AC3 — Documented.** The installer's own documentation and the hook-wiring
  docs state the dependency on the resolved `wl` and how to refresh it
  (`docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` global-install section,
  `docs/dev/context-budget.md` hook-wiring section, `README.md` install entry
  as needed).
  *Verification:* each touched page names the `wl`-refresh step (or the new
  guard) and the failure it prevents.

## Candidate remedies (pros / cons)

**(a) Detect a `ContextHub` checkout and rebuild (or reinstall) the global `wl`
during install.** Resolve the global `worklog` link target; if it is inside a
git checkout, run `npm run build` there (or `npm link`/`npm i -g` when the link
is absent).
- *Pros:* removes the root cause on developer machines; one command still sets
  everything up; no new convention for consuming repos.
- *Cons:* gives a global installer a cross-repo build responsibility (slow,
  needs the link target's dependencies and a working toolchain); it builds
  whatever branch/dirty state that checkout happens to be on, so it can install
  the *wrong* template just as silently; surprising side effect for anyone who
  did not expect the installer to mutate `../ContextHub`.

**(b) Pin an explicit `worklog` version and refuse to run against an unexpected
one.** Commit the expected version (e.g. in the project's installer config or
`package.json`) and have the installer compare it with `wl --version`.
- *Pros:* deterministic and fail-loud; makes the dependency visible in every
  repo; cheap to implement; no cross-repo mutation.
- *Cons:* version numbers do not prove template equality — two builds of
  `1.0.27` can carry different templates, which is exactly the observed hazard;
  a mismatch blocks the operator until they rebuild by hand; needs a per-repo
  convention to keep the pin current.

**(c) Fail loudly when the installed template predates the committed hook.**
Compare the template the resolved `wl` would emit
(`wl init`-equivalent content, e.g. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`
hook content, or a `wl hooks print`-style helper) against the repo's committed
`.githooks/pre-push`; refuse (or warn with the exact remedy) when the committed
hook carries capability the template lacks.
- *Pros:* cheap and directly targeted at the silent-deletion mechanism; needs no
  version convention; naturally testable in the existing installer test with a
  stub `wl`; fail-loud, and can be made fail-soft-visible (`WARNING`) where a
  hard failure would be hostile.
- *Cons:* if implemented only in the installer it is an *install-time* guard —
  a later manual `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` bypasses it, so the durable
  "never downgrade a hook" guard belongs upstream in
  `ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` (with its own test) and this item
  should file that as a linked upstream item rather than assume it here.

### Recommendation

Implement **(c)** in the installer (fail-loud skew check, hermetic test,
documentation), because it is the smallest change that removes the silent
deletion path and it is testable in the existing installer suite. Follow it with
**(b)** as a cheap visibility convention (expected `worklog` version recorded
where the installer can read it), noting explicitly in the docs that the version
is a hint, not proof. Treat **(a)** as an **opt-in** flag
(`--refresh-wl`/`PI_REFRESH_WL=1`) rather than default behaviour, and file the
durable upstream guard (refuse a template "downgrade" inside `upgradeHooks`)
against `ContextHub` where the destructive write actually lives.

## Tests & documentation (explicitly in scope)

- This is a **shared framework script**, so the change cannot ship without
  tests: extend `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` (existing, ~15 KB) with
  sandboxed-`HOME` cases — stale template + divergent committed hook
  (refusal/warning), up-to-date template (silent OK), `wl` absent (`wl`-not-found
  path must remain non-fatal, as the installer is fail-open elsewhere), and the
  opt-in refresh flag if (a) is taken.
- Documentation is part of the deliverable, not a follow-up: the installer's
  install notes, `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (global install),
  `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (hook wiring) and the `README.md` install entry
  must describe the `wl` dependency and the remedy.
- Any "never downgrade" guard added in `ContextHub` needs its own test there
  (`../ContextHub/tests/`), as a separate `WL-` item.

## Key Files

- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — hook-wiring block (:317-412); the place a skew check
  / opt-in refresh belongs.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` — the installer hook-wiring suite the
  new cases extend (sandboxed `HOME`).
- `../ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` — `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` and
  `upgradeHooks()` (:603-643, whole-file overwrite at :622) — the durable
  "never downgrade" guard target (separate `WL-` item).
- `../ContextHub/src/commands/doctor/upgrade.ts` — the `--dry-run` / `--confirm`
  CLI contract a dry-run-based skew check would consume.
- `../ContextHub/.gitignore` — line 86 (`dist`), the reason the template is not
  version-controlled.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`, `docs/dev/context-budget.md`, `README.md` —
  documentation surface.

## Constraints

- The installer is shared across every framework project and must stay
  **fail-open** for non-hook concerns (it already warns rather than dies on a
  missing context-audit skill, missing thresholds, or a failed identity guard);
  only the hook-template skew guard may be fail-loud, and its exit behaviour
  needs an explicit decision (blocking vs `WARNING`) recorded in the item.
- No live-`HOME` mutations in tests: sandbox `HOME` (as the existing suite does).
- Do not rebuild a `ContextHub` checkout the operator did not ask to rebuild
  (option (a) must be opt-in), and never mutate another repository from a
  default install.
- Push to `dev` only, never `main`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the resolved `wl` on a framework host is the npm-linked
  `ContextHub` build (verified above); a registry install would make (a)
  meaningless but (c)/(b) still useful.
- **Risk:** a `wl` that cannot print its template (e.g. an older `wl` without a
  print path) forces the check to parse `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` or
  to fall back to a version comparison — the fallback must be documented and
  must not turn into a hard failure on an old `wl`.
- **Risk:** failing the whole install on skew could block a machine whose only
  problem is a stale `dist`; prefer an actionable `WARNING` plus a clear remedy
  unless the producer prefers a hard failure.
- **Risk:** duplicate coverage with `CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU`'s AC2 tail clause —
  that item explicitly records the gap and does **not** fix it, so this item is
  the fix, not a duplicate.

## Related work

- `CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — discovered-from; the
  template-ownership item whose AC2 tail clause records this gap.
- `WL-0MW20XXWE00466FP` (ContextHub) — the upstream template change
  (`mirror_suite_cache`), the capability whose silent removal motivated this.
- `SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM` (completed) — an earlier `install_pi.sh` hook-scope
  defect (v3 gate propagated to non-SorraAgents projects); same block, same
  fail-open principle.
- `SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG` (completed) — "Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md
  after git pull": the same stale-`dist` failure mode documented for agents,
  fixed by documentation rather than by an installer guard.
- `SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX` (completed) — the installer's git-identity guard, the
  precedent for "surface the problem at install time, fail-open".

## Deliverables

- `scripts/install_pi.sh` skew check (or opt-in refresh flag, per the recorded
  decision) with fail-loud/`WARNING` output naming both hook versions.
- New cases in `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` (sandboxed `HOME`).
- Documentation updates in the installer's install notes,
  `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`, `docs/dev/context-budget.md`, `README.md`.
- A linked `WL-` item for the durable upstream "never downgrade" guard in
  `upgradeHooks()` (filed, not implemented here).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-17 — Plan decomposition created 4 child items (test-first order):
  - `SA-0MWK5QU4H003S85S` — Test: skew-detection cases for install_pi hook wiring (AC2)
  - `SA-0MWK8D4OG004Z4ZB` — Implement: template skew check in install_pi.sh hook wiring (AC1)
  - `SA-0MWK8D5T0005PVR7` — Docs: document wl dependency and template skew guard (AC3)
  - `SA-0MWK8D6Z90005O7V` — Discover: file linked WL item for upstream never-downgrade guard
- Dependencies wired: Implement→Test; Docs→Implement; Discover WL item→Implement (test-first slicing).
- AC coverage review: 100% (3/3 parent ACs covered), recommendation `proceed`.
- Effort/risk estimate: Small / Medium (expected 10.17h, recommended 16.17h; risk score 6/25).

data.description:
# Refactor skill: REFACTOR markers cross-wired and added without a fix

**Headline:** The 2026-11-06 scheduled `/skill:refactor` run wrote
`REFACTOR-<id>` markers whose work-item id belonged to a *different* file, and
wrote them into files it never changed. The positional mis-pairing itself is
already fixed in code (identity-keyed mapping, b05cbad554 /
SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG), but nothing pins that fix and nothing stops a future
mis-pairing from reaching disk. This item adds the missing regression coverage,
a fail-closed identity check before a marker is written, and a marker block
that states the smell is pre-existing and unfixed.

## Problem statement

A scheduled full-project refactor run injected marker-only edits into files the
run had not changed, carrying ids of work items that named *other* files; the
genuine mechanical fixes landed elsewhere with no marker at all. Release prep
had to revert the two marker-only hunks (b536b9dbe) before the tree could be
shipped, and the mismatch made the scan report untrustworthy.

## Users

- **Producers running `/skill:refactor`** (directly or via the scheduler) — they
  read the injected markers as "this file still carries tracked debt"; a
  cross-wired marker sends them to the wrong file.
- **Implementation agents** working a refactor item — they trust the marker in
  the file named by the item, and are misled when the marker names a foreign
  item or the item's own file carries no marker.
- **Release/prep agents** — marker-only hunks with no accompanying fix are
  indistinguishable from real changes and block or churn a release.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when a refactor run annotates a file, I want the marker's work
  item to name exactly that file, so that following the marker leads me to the
  right fix."
- "As a release agent, when I see a marker-only diff, I want the marker itself
  to say the smell is pre-existing and unfixed, so that I do not treat the hunk
  as an attempted fix that failed."

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pipeline-level regression test exercises `remediate_pre_existing()` with a
  smell batch shaped like the 2026-11-06 incident (one identity group skipped or
  collapsed to `None` before a later group's injection) and fails on the
  positional-index implementation: every injected `REFACTOR-<id>` marker must
  carry the id the batch filed for *that* smell's finding identity, and no
  marker may be written outside the file its work item names.
- Marker injection is fail-closed on identity: before writing, the resolved
  work item's identity (its `Refactor-Finding-Key` when present, otherwise the
  file path recorded in its title/description) is compared with the smell's
  `<code>:<repository-relative path>`; a mismatch writes nothing, logs a
  warning, and increments a mismatch counter surfaced in both the JSON report
  and the human-readable scan summary.
- A legacy item without a `Refactor-Finding-Key` marker (e.g. one whose
  description was rewritten by intake) still receives its marker through the
  title/description path fallback, so verification never silently drops a
  correctly paired marker.
- The injected marker block states that the smell is pre-existing and unfixed
  (an additive `state:` line), so a marker-only edit documents why it
  accompanies no code change; the existing parsers (`REFACTOR_PATTERN`,
  `REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN`, `has_existing_smell_comment`) and the planned
  stale-marker removal sweep still match the block.
- Unit tests cover the identity-verification helper (matching item, mismatched
  item, legacy item without a marker, absent item) and parser compatibility of
  the new `state:` line.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (marker block format, verification
  behaviour, cross-wiring failure mode), and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A refactor run can only annotate the file its work item names, and every marker
it leaves behind says plainly that the smell is pre-existing and unfixed — so a
marker-only diff can no longer be mistaken for a fix or land in the wrong file.

## Constraints

- No retroactive edits to history: the two reverted hunks (b536b9dbe) stay
  reverted; no existing marker in the tree is rewritten by this item.
- The `state:` line must be additive — the marker's first line stays
  `REFACTOR-<id>` and the `smell:` line stays in its current position, so
  removal/sweep tooling (SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9, SA-0MWFW1ZDT006VYM4) and the
  two existing regexes keep working.
- Verification must be cheap: at most one extra `wl show`/`wl list` lookup per
  injected marker, and no new dependency on network or LLM calls.
- No behaviour change to auto-fix, smell detection, or item creation; only the
  marker-write path and its reporting change.
- The canonical source is this repository (`skill/refactor/`); the installed
  copy under `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor` is a symlink and is never edited.
- All work-item bookkeeping uses `wl`; no edits to
  `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl`.
- Test execution goes through `/skill:test` (never ad-hoc pytest).

## Existing state

- **Root cause (already fixed):** before b05cbad554 (`SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG`,
  "Machine-readable finding identity marker", landed 2026-11-13),
  `remediate_pre_existing()` paired work-item ids to smells **positionally**:
  `smell_index = smells.index(smell); created_ids[smell_index]`. Because
  `create_smell_work_items()` omits skipped/failed groups, any skip shifted
  every later pairing by one. On 2026-11-06 (`22:06`) that produced exactly the
  observed cross-wiring: `skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py`
  received `REFACTOR-SA-0MW5IZN330071FQU` (the item for
  `tests/test_implement_drive_worktree_cleanup.py`) and
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_green_run.py` received
  `REFACTOR-SA-0MW5IZLES00362FK` (the item for
  `skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py`).
- The fix replaced positional pairing with
  `create_smell_work_items_mapped()` + `created_map.get(build_finding_key(smell))`
  (`skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py`, `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py`).
- **No test pins the pairing.** Nothing under `tests/test_refactor/` references
  `create_smell_work_items_mapped`; `remediate_pre_existing` is only mocked in
  `tests/test_refactor/test_auto_fix.py`. A regression to positional pairing
  would pass the current suite.
- `inject_refactor_comment()` (`skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`) writes the
  block at the file head (below a shebang) after only a duplicate-by-smell-type
  check; it never verifies that `work_item_id` actually tracks this file, so a
  wrong id is written silently.
- The block content is `REFACTOR-<id>` / `smell:` / `severity:` /
  `description:` with no statement about fix state, which is why a marker-only
  hunk reads like an attempted fix.
- Legacy refactor items whose descriptions were rewritten (e.g.
  `SA-0MWI3MT6L004K1L7`) do not carry `Refactor-Finding-Key`; its own
  OPEN QUESTION records that gap. Verification therefore cannot rely on the
  marker alone.

## Desired change

- Extract the identity resolution used by `_find_existing_worklog_item` so the
  injection path can resolve an item's identity in one place (marker first,
  title/description file-path fallback second).
- In `remediate_pre_existing()`, verify the pairing before calling
  `inject_refactor_comment()`; on mismatch skip the write, log, and count it in
  a new `comment_identity_mismatches` field in the report dict.
- Add the `state: pre-existing, not fixed` line to `_build_comment_block()`
  output (both block and line-prefixed styles) and assert parser compatibility.
- Add `tests/test_refactor/test_marker_pairing.py` (name indicative) with the
  incident-shaped regression test plus verification-helper unit tests.
- Document the marker block, the verification step and the cross-wiring failure
  mode in `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — `remediate_pre_existing()`: identity
  verification before injection, mismatch counter in the report dict.
- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — `_build_comment_block()`: additive
  `state:` line; `inject_refactor_comment()`: identity-guard hook.
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — shared helper that resolves a work
  item's finding identity (marker or path fallback), reused by the guard.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_marker_pairing.py` — new pipeline-level
  cross-wiring regression tests.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — `state:` line and parser
  compatibility tests.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_workitem_creation.py` — identity-resolution unit
  tests (marker, legacy fallback, absent).
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — marker block format, verification, failure mode.

## Related work

- `SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG` (completed) — introduced the identity marker and the
  identity-keyed mapping that already fixes the positional mis-pairing. This
  item adds the regression coverage and the write-time guard it left out.
- `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` (open) — removes stale `REFACTOR` markers when their
  work item closes; the `state:` line must stay compatible with its parser.
- `SA-0MVVF468O009TAIF` (open) — marker placement relative to shebang/encoding
  line/docstring; same write path, so ordering must be agreed but not re-solved
  here.
- `SA-0MVNBEPHH009LB5X` (open) — the report claims unfixed diagnostics as
  auto-fixes; complementary trust defect in the same report.
- `SA-0MVZHMZBU005FEJN` (open) — `remediate_pre_existing()` drops skipped
  findings silently inside the same `comment_errors` counter; the new
  `comment_identity_mismatches` counter must compose with that item's
  per-finding skip reasons rather than duplicate them.
- `SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3` (open) — re-verification of linter-derived items
  (consumes `Refactor-Fingerprint`).
- `SA-0MVZA21600087VRD`, `SA-0MWFW20O2008AG91`, `SA-0MWFW2389003HHVE` (open /
  blocked) — marker sweep family; parsers must stay compatible.
- `SA-0MWI3MT6L004K1L7` (open) — example legacy item with no
  `Refactor-Finding-Key`; motivates the path fallback.
- Discovery record: `SA-0MW5KI5FH004OK7O` (completed) — release prep that
  reverted the cross-wired marker-only hunks in b536b9dbe.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (recorded, producer to confirm):** the second expectation
  ("a marker must only accompany an actual fix, or explicitly document why no
  fix is applied") is satisfied by the additive `state: pre-existing, not
  fixed` line rather than by suppressing markers for unfixed smells — markers
  exist to track *unfixed* pre-existing debt, so suppressing them would remove
  the skill's dedupe signal. See Appendix Q1.
- **Risk:** a strict verification guard could skip legacy items en masse. The
  path fallback plus a reported (not silent) mismatch count mitigates this;
  the mismatch counter makes any systematic skip visible in the scan report.
- **Risk of scope creep:** the marker lifecycle (removal, re-verification,
  placement) has four sibling items; this item must not absorb them.
- **Risk:** an extra `wl show` per marker could slow full-project scans;
  mitigated by resolving identity once per group rather than per smell, and by
  keeping the guard subprocess count bounded.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (OPEN QUESTION — producer decision required).** The item's second
  expectation reads "a marker must only accompany an actual fix (or explicitly
  document why no fix is applied)". Markers are injected for *pre-existing,
  unfixed* smells by design, so which reading applies?
  - (a) Keep injecting markers for unfixed smells, and have the block state
    `state: pre-existing, not fixed` so a marker-only hunk is self-documenting.
  - (b) Stop injecting markers into files the run did not modify (markers only
    for session-scoped scans or only for files the auto-fix step touched).
  - (c) Keep markers as-is and rely on the run report/commit message to state
    that the markers accompany no fix.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — smallest behavioural change, keeps the dedupe signal

    comments into source files to track pre-existing…") and
    `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`; (b) would silently remove duplicate suppression
    for every full-project scan.

    producer response yet. The brief and ACs proceed on the recommended option
    (a) so implementation is not blocked, and option (b) is reachable by
    dropping AC4 and gating injection on the modified-file set.
- **Q2.** Is the identity-keyed mapping from b05cbad554
  (`SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG`) accepted as the root-cause fix, so this item carries
  only regression coverage plus the write-time guard?
  - Answer (agent, from repository evidence): yes — `git show b05cbad554` shows

# Standup more focused on user experience (re-homed from ContextHub)

> **Provenance:** re-homed from ContextHub epic WL-0MW397N0Z002AYWP per producer
> decision (Option A). The standup skill source of truth lives in this
> (SorraAgents) repository — `skill/standup/` — which `~/.pi/agent/skills`
> symlinks to. The ContextHub copy is closed as moved.


## Problem statement

The daily standup report is currently a dry, flat bullet list of work items
("things done" + technical summaries), which is hard to read aloud and does
not convey what the user gained from the work. The output should be grouped
into meaningful categories, with each completed item described as a
single sentence about its impact on the user experience — without work item
IDs.

## Users

- The operator, who reads/listens to the daily standup (TTS) and wants a
  readable narrative of what changed and why it matters to the user.
- Agent sessions that generate standups and need clear, stable instructions
  for turning the script's structured data into the grouped report.

Example user stories:
- "As the operator, I want the standup grouped by areas such as 'User
  experience when doing Foo' and 'Back end stability under heavy load', so I
  can quickly grasp where progress happened and what each change means for
  users."
- "As the operator, I want each completed item described as one
  user-experience impact sentence without IDs, e.g. 'Improved the speed of
  user interactions with Foo by providing a one-click setup of the deck'."

## Desired change

1. **Categories** are chosen by the LLM (the invoking agent) at report time;
   labels are free-form (e.g. "User experience when doing Foo", "UI layout to
   improve access to key information"). No fixed taxonomy.
2. **Per-item impact sentences** come from a new explicit `## Impact` line in
   the work item description, written by the agent completing the work. Items
   without one (including all existing legacy items, which are **not**
   retrofitted) fall back to the current `Title — user story` phrasing.
3. **Grouped-paragraph format in every section** — "Yesterday I completed work
   on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus items for today",
   "Regressions" and "Blockers" — each section grouped **independently**
   (categories are chosen per section, not per whole report).
4. The deterministic script (`generate_standup.py`) continues to fetch and
   compute the selection data; it also extracts each item's `## Impact`
   sentence into the structured output. The LLM (agent session) does the
   clustering and paragraph rendering, keeping the script testable and the
   agent output interpretable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `generate_standup.py` extracts the `## Impact` sentence from each item's
   description into a dedicated structured field (e.g. `impact`), available in
   `--json` output; a missing/malformed Impact section yields an empty field
   without error.
2. The rendered report is readable as a narrative: it organises each section's
   items into categories chosen by the LLM at report time, items are grouped
   **independently within each section**, and no work item IDs appear anywhere
   in the rendered report.
3. Within each category, every item is described as a single
   user-experience-focused sentence: the item's `## Impact` sentence when
   present, else the existing `Title — user story` phrasing (fallback).
4. The report remains first-person and TTS-friendly (spoken-form dates, no
   ID brackets/backticks/underscores in spoken lines) and stays within the
   ~2-minute read budget.
5. CLI behaviour is unchanged for consumers (flags, JSON schema superset,
   `--output-path` write path, sync-first, commit/push); existing tests keep
   passing with additions for the new `impact` extraction.
6. Work-item completion guidance (project AGENTS.md / implement skill / intake
   brief template) is updated so newly completed items carry an `## Impact`
   sentence describing the user-experience impact of the change.
7. Testing/validation: unit tests cover Impact extraction (present, absent,
   malformed) and the fallback; a golden-output test renders a sample report
   and asserts grouped sections, no IDs, and Impact-first sentences.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, the standup SKILL.md, and any wiki/docs entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The script stays deterministic (no LLM calls inside `generate_standup.py`) —
  clustering/rendering happens in the invoking agent session per Q4 answer.
- Existing completed items are NOT retrofitted with `## Impact` lines.
- Report must stay first-person, TTS-friendly, under ~2 minutes reading time.
- No work item IDs in the rendered output.
- Surgical scope: the Herdr selection ordering and data sources are untouched.

## Existing state

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (installed to
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/`) renders a flat markdown report from the
  Herdr selection list; per-item text is `Title — user story/problem/summary`
  extracted heuristically from the description.
- Report structure: `## <project> Standup Report (date)` with sections
  "Yesterday I completed work on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus
  items for today", "Regressions", "Blockers".
- Items already carry `Key Files` and (mostly) `As a …` user stories in their
  descriptions; there is no standard Impact field today.

## Desired change (implementation sketch)

- `generate_standup.py`: add `extract_impact(description)` (parse the
  `## Impact` section) and include `impact` in `normalize_item`/report data;
  keep `format_report` as a stable fallback for `--json` consumers and tests.
- `skill/standup/SKILL.md`: replace the "Report Structure" template with
  agent-rendered instructions: cluster each section's items into free-form
  categories, render one paragraph per category (one impact sentence per
  item), never render IDs, keep the TTS/first-person rules, note the
  `## Impact` / fallback rule.
- Work-item authoring guidance: add `## Impact` (one sentence,
  user-experience impact) to the completion conventions (implement skill
  output / AGENTS.md), so future standups have real impact sentences.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/SKILL.md` — report template → clustered paragraph
  rendering instructions; source of truth `skill/standup/SKILL.md` in the
  SorraAgents repo.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — add `## Impact`
  extraction + `impact` structured field; keep JSON/fallback compat.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_*.py` — new tests for
  Impact extraction, fallback, no-ID golden output.
- `AGENTS.md` (project + `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` global) / intake brief
  template — completed items gain an `## Impact` sentence.

## Related work

- **Create a podcast for standups (WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8)** — consumes the
  rendered standup report; ensuring the grouped narrative stays parseable/TTS-
  friendly matters for it.
- Completed standup infra (sync-first WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K, maintenance
  routines WL-0MVIDWJ090090J3Q, scheduled prompts WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR) —
  unchanged; this is an output-format change.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: existing items are not retrofitted with Impact lines (fallback
  covers them). Confirmed by operator (Q5/A).
- Assumption: LLM clustering runs in the invoking agent session, not in the
  script (Q4/A). Risk: agent non-determinism → mitigations: keep deterministic
  data layer, document expected structure, golden output reviewed in tests at
  the data layer, SKILL.md instructions constrain clustering.
- Risk: paragraphs lengthen the report past 2 minutes → mitigation: the agent
  is instructed to keep each category paragraph tight and cap per-item
  sentences at one.
- Risk: Impact lines may be missing or low-quality → fallback + guidance
  update (AC6); scope-creep risk noted: no changes to Herdr selection or
  podcast pipeline (linked as related work, not scope).
- Risk: agents may accidentally include IDs → explicit "no IDs" rule in
  SKILL.md + golden-output test asserting absence (AC2).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should categories be determined?" — Answer (operator): "C — LLM-chosen at report time (free-form labels)". Source: interactive reply (round 1, 2026-11-06).
- Q2: "Where does each item's impact sentence come from?" — Answer (operator): "A — explicit `## Impact` line written into work items at completion; the script reads it". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "Which sections get the new grouped-paragraph format?" — Answer (operator): "C — every section, but group independently within the sections". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q4: "Where does the LLM clustering run?" — Answer (operator): "A — in the invoking agent session; script emits structured item data; SKILL.md instructs the agent to cluster and render". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Q5: "Items without an `## Impact` line?" — Answer (operator): "A — fall back to current Title — user story phrasing". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Assumption (confirmed implicitly): existing completed items are not retrofitted with Impact lines.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRMG8P2X004V6YC** – help line for chord commands too verbose (completed)
- **WL-0MQZX8BTN006N4BF** – Automatically recover from appropriate server errors (completed)
- **WL-0MURJ0LFH002O95I** – r-i (Producer Interview) should focus on the created pane (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: access, back, category, click, completed, currently, defined, discovery, dry, end, etc, example, fit, focused, foo, group, heavy, ids, information, key, layout, lets, list, load, one, output, paragraph, providing, readable, see, should, single, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: access, achieve, back, completed, currently, defined, describing, doing, end, etc, example, fit, focused, foo, group, ids, impact, improve, key, layout, list, load, one, output, paragraph, readable, see, setup, should, single, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: back, completed, defined, discovery, dry, easy, end, etc, fit, focused, foo, group, heavy, ids, improve, improved, key, list, load, one, output, readable, see, setup, should, single, speed, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-06: Plan decomposition complete (plan skill). 7 child work items created in test-first dependency order. AC coverage: 100%. Key Files validated.
  - WL-0MW5HUS5E001SG6H — Unit tests for Impact extraction
  - WL-0MW5HVPJP009MVPQ — Impact extraction implementation in generate_standup.py
  - WL-0MW5HVQ7Z006SI6Q — Impact-aware report rendering + TTS fallback
  - WL-0MW5HVQY30018XZR — Golden-output test for grouped no-ID report
  - WL-0MW5HVRPJ002OOCH — Update standup SKILL.md for agent-rendered clustered report

# Intake Brief — Audit runner leaves stale `pending-screens.json` when no child screens remain

## Problem statement

The audit runner clears its in-memory view of pending child screens but does **not** delete (or empty) the on-disk `<issue_id>.pending-screens.json` signal when the collected pending set for a run is empty. Because `cmd_issue` bypasses the freshness fast-path while that file names any child, a stale signal forces every later audit of the item to re-run the whole Phase 1 pipeline (one model call each) even though nothing is pending — a silent, repeatable cost that contradicts the documented "cleared automatically once none remain" contract.

## Users

- **Operators/agents auditing a parent item** whose child screens were already resolved (child closed as duplicate, fixed upstream, or serviced in a prior run) — they re-audit an item that is genuinely settled and unexpectedly pay for a full pipeline run each time.
- **The herdr downtime dispatcher** — dispatch-driven audits inherit the same wasted-cost path when a signal lingers.
- **Maintainers reading the audit docs** — the documented resume/clear contract currently overstates actual behaviour.

Example user stories:

- As an operator re-auditing `CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE` after closing its only child, I want the stale signal removed so the next audit takes the freshness fast-path instead of re-running Phase 1.
- As a maintainer, I want a closed child to never be persisted into the pending-screens signal, so the signal can only ever name screens that can still be serviced.

## Observed behaviour (reproduction)

Observed on 2026-11-09 auditing `CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE` (Tableau-Card-Engine):

1. Run 1 (default in-main-slot mode) emitted one child screen for `CG-0MW97UZ68001JTGK` and wrote `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE.pending-screens.json`.
2. The child was then closed (duplicate; failure fixed upstream).
3. Resume run reported `"pending_child_screens": []` and a `Ready to close: Yes` verdict, **but the signal file remained**, still naming the closed child.
4. Workaround applied at the time: the stale file was deleted by hand so the next audit could take the freshness fast-path.

## Existing state / root cause (verified in tree)

The signal write and the reported pending set are derived from **two different predicates**, so they can disagree:

- The `--json` payload / readiness gate computes `pending_child_screens` as `_pending_main_slot_child_ids(child_results)` **minus** `_unserviced_main_slot_child_ids(child_results, stale_pending_ids)` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~`:10540`).
- The signal write at the report-assembly site calls `_write_pending_screens_signal(_pending_main_slot_child_ids(child_results), …)` — **unfiltered** (`:16747`–`:16756`). `_write_pending_screens_signal` does unlink when it receives an empty list (`:8005`), so it only stays stale when it receives a non-empty list.
- On a checkpoint resume, `active_children` excludes only `deleted` (`:15641`), so a child closed as `completed`/`done` **stays** in the restored `child_results` still carrying the `partial` + `main-session review` pending marker. `_re_resolve_pending_main_slot_children` cannot re-resolve a closed-as-duplicate child (no own stored audit), so it is left carrying the placeholder (`:15526`).
- Net effect: the closed child is subtracted from the reported `pending_child_screens` (it is "unserviced", `:10542`) yet re-written into the signal (unfiltered, `:16753`) — exactly the observed "JSON says `[]`, file still names the child".

Secondary path worth covering: any early-return / short-circuit that never reaches the report-assembly write (freshness fast-path at `:13364`–`:13377`, dry-run freshness refresh guard at `:17593`) also leaves an existing stale file untouched.

Documented contract it violates: `skill/audit/SKILL.md:233` and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md:1226` both state the signal "is cleared/deleted automatically once none remain".

## Desired change

Make the on-disk signal a faithful mirror of the screens that can still be serviced:

1. Derive **both** the reported `pending_child_screens` and the signal contents from a **single** shared helper so they cannot diverge.
2. A child that is closed (`status=completed`/`stage=done`) or `deleted` must **never** be persisted into the signal — it can never be serviced by a later run.
3. When the resulting signal set is empty, the file is removed (existing `unlink(missing_ok=True)` path) on **both** the fresh-run and resume paths, including the short-circuit paths that currently skip the write.
4. Genuinely outstanding screens are unchanged: an **open**, unserviced child still keeps the signal (and therefore the freshness-gate bypass + resume behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When the collected pending set for a run is empty, `<issue_id>.pending-screens.json` is removed from the checkpoint directory on both the fresh-run and the resume path — the file does not survive a run whose JSON payload reports `"pending_child_screens": []`.
- AC2: A child that is closed (`status=completed`/`stage=done`) or `deleted` is never written into the signal; the signal only ever names children whose screens can still be serviced.
- AC3: Genuinely pending screens are unaffected — with an open, unserviced child still outstanding, the signal survives and still lists that child, and the freshness-gate bypass / checkpoint-resume contract still collects a serviced child with zero child `pi` calls.
- AC4 (validation): Regression tests prove (a) resume with the named child closed ⇒ signal removed and payload `pending_child_screens == []`; (b) fresh run with a closed child ⇒ no signal written; (c) control: an open unserviced child ⇒ signal present and naming that child. Tests exercise the real `_write_pending_screens_signal` / report-assembly path with `wl`/`pi` mocked (no real subprocess, no self-referential re-implementation of game/audit logic).
- AC5: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries — stating precisely when the signal is cleared and which children it can name.
- AC6: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators re-auditing a parent whose child screens are already resolved stop paying for a full Phase 1 re-run on every audit, because a resolved child can no longer leave a signal that permanently bypasses the freshness fast-path.

## Constraints

- Surgical change confined to the audit runner's signal derivation; no behaviour change for genuinely outstanding screens (AC3).
- Do **not** fix this by subtracting every `_unserviced_main_slot_child_ids` entry — that would clear the signal for genuinely unserviced *open* children, re-clamping the item on the freshness fast-path and losing the resume.
- `--no-checkpoint` behaviour is unchanged (it reads/writes no signal).
- Manual deletion of stale files is the existing workaround, not the fix.
- Bulk sweeping of already-stale signals across project worklogs is out of scope (tracked by SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS).
- UK English in all written output.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** a closed (`completed`/`done`) or `deleted` child can never need an in-main-slot screen, so it must never appear in the signal. Implementation should confirm against the production case (child closed as duplicate).
- **Risk — over-clearing:** naively subtracting all unserviced ids clears signals for open unserviced children. Mitigation: drop only children that can never be serviced (closed/deleted) or are provably resolved; keep the helper's identity test explicit.
- **Risk — re-divergence:** two predicates is the bug class. Mitigation: one helper feeds both the report/JSON set and the signal set (AC1/AC2).
- **Risk — scope creep:** the 43-signal cross-project sweep belongs to SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS; record any extra opportunity as a linked item, not scope here.
- **Assumption:** the send/clear contract stays "signal names only serviceable screens", so the docs are corrected to match tightened behaviour rather than rewritten.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_pending_main_slot_child_ids` (~:7960), `_write_pending_screens_signal` (~:7984), `_is_unserviced_main_slot_child` (~:8028), `_unserviced_main_slot_child_ids` (~:8119), `_read_pending_screens_signal` (~:8182); call site ~:16747–:16756; reported `pending_child_screens` ~:10540; freshness fast-path ~:13364–:13377; dry-run refresh guard ~:17593.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — extend the existing resume-clears-signal coverage (`test_resume_then_report_clears_gate_and_signal` ~:1300, `_write_signal` helper ~:407) with the closed-child case and the open-child control.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (:233) — child-audit execution contract wording.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (:1226) — resumable-signal contract wording.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S** (completed) — in-main-slot child-screen resume (D1 freshness gate + D2 checkpoint replay); the resume cycle this bug sits on top of.
- **SA-0MU32TE120012T49** (completed) — introduced the resumable pending-screens signal and the "cleared automatically when none remain" contract.
- **SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45** (completed) — unserviced in-main-slot verdict handling; source of the `unserviced_ids` subtraction that the signal write omits.
- **SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM** (completed) — re-resolve pending children on checkpoint resume; the reconcile path that cannot re-resolve a closed child.
- **SA-0MW2J7NGP006CIEG** (completed) — made the freshness gate pending-screens aware (the bypass a stale file keeps triggering).
- **SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS** (open) — one-off operational sweep of stale signals; explicitly defers the root-cause guard to this item.
- **SA-0MW2J8G260045D17** (open) — dispatched audits should not emit unserviceable screens; adjacent (a dispatched audit produces exactly the unserviced state this signal bug then pins).

Automated find-related report (`find-related`): related work items SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM, SA-0MU32TE120012T49, SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS; repository matches `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (plus a loose `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` match, not relevant). Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Note:** the seed context was complete — problem, impact, reproduction, expected vs actual, and the manual workaround were all supplied — and the root cause was confirmed by reading the tree. No requirement-discovery interview was needed; the entries below record the research that stood in for it.

- **Q (self-resolved by repo research): where does the signal get written?** Answer: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` `_write_pending_screens_signal` (~:7984), called once at report assembly (~:16752) with the **unfiltered** `_pending_main_slot_child_ids(child_results)`. Evidence: `grep -n "_write_pending_screens_signal"` → definition + single call site.
- **Q: why does the payload report `[]` while the file persists?** Answer: the payload subtracts `unserviced_ids` (~:10540–:10543) but the signal write does not (~:16753); a closed-as-duplicate child stays in restored `child_results` with the pending marker and is classified unserviced. Evidence: tree read of `_unserviced_main_slot_child_ids` (~:8119), `_re_resolve_pending_main_slot_children` (~:15505) and `active_children` filter (~:15641).
- **Q: is this a duplicate of the sweep item?** Answer: no — SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS is an operational sweep and states "the root-cause guard against stale leftovers is SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU and stays out of scope here." Evidence: `wl show SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS --json` constraints section.
- **Q: does a documented contract need changing?** Answer: no — both docs already state the signal is "cleared automatically once none remain"; the implementation diverges, so the docs need precision (which children may be named), not a behaviour change. Evidence: `skill/audit/SKILL.md:233`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md:1226`.

## Intake CLI: check-filing subcommand and flags

### Goal
Add check-filing subcommand to intake.py and wire it as step 0c after claim. Add CLI flags for misfiled-item handling.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. skill:intake runs a filing-location check for the target work item before any other mutation, and reports its findings to the operator (stderr plus work-item comment). The check is non-blocking: intake proceeds whether or not the item passes the check.
2. On a non-ok classification the script logs a warning and records an idempotent filing location check comment on the item (re-runs update the existing comment, never duplicate). When stdin is an interactive TTY it additionally offers continue or recreate the item in the correct project. Auto-recreation is only possible via an explicit --misfiled-action recreate flag and never happens by default.
3. Recreating (when chosen) creates a new item under the target project's store/prefix copying title, description, tags, issue type and priority, records a Recreated from source-id reference, and closes the original with the reason Misfiled: recreated in target-project (target-id). A dry-run --dry-run mode prints the would-be recreation without creating.
4. intake.py gains a check-filing <id> subcommand that runs the filing check.
5. check-filing runs as step 0c right after claim in the intake flow.
6. CLI gains --misfiled-action {warn,offer,recreate} (default warn), --recreate-target <project-dir>, and --dry-run flags.
7. No other skill's behavior changes in this work item.
8. The check is non-blocking - intake proceeds whether or not the item passes.
9. Idempotent - re-running the check on the same item yields the same result and never duplicates comments or recreations.
10. Legitimate cross-project usage stays quiet - running intake from the SorraAgents checkout on a WL- item routed by prefix-to-sibling scan is supported behaviour.

### Key Files
- skill/intake/scripts/intake.py - check-filing subcommand + hookup
- skill/shared/filing_location.py - invoked by check-filing

# Remote-observed push verdict in finish

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Builds on the test-first slice (the hermetic baselines land first; this slice makes them pass
and removes their `xfail(strict=True)` markers).

## Goal

As an implementation agent, when the push command is killed at the timeout but `origin/dev`
already points at my commit, I want `finish` to record the completion comment and leave the
item `completed`/`in_review` instead of resetting it to `open`; and as the producer, when
`finish` does report a push failure I want the report to say whether the commit was verified
**absent** from `origin/dev` or whether verification itself could not run, so I know exactly
what recovery is needed.

## Context

`git_push_to_dev()` (`implement.py` L5629) spawns `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` in
its own process group. On `TimeoutExpired` it process-group-kills the push and raises
`PushTimeoutError` (L4667); on a non-zero exit it raises `PushNonFastForwardError` for
non-fast-forward wording, otherwise logs `git push to dev failed` and returns `False`. There is
no post-failure remote check. `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011) maps a `False` return to
`RuntimeError("git push to dev failed.")`, posts a manual-push comment on `PushTimeoutError`,
and the outer `RuntimeError` handler resets the status to `open`; steps 6a–8 (post-push
ancestry assertion, cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync) and the
`StatusLifecycle(target_stage="in_review")` exit run only after a successful push.
`_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050) retries the push inside the worktree and has the
same false-failure exposure.

## Desired change

1. Add `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout=...) -> bool | None`: resolve the
   full hash, read `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetch that ref when the
   tip differs (bounded), and return `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says the commit
   is reachable, `False` when positively absent, `None` when the probe itself failed
   (network/auth/timeout).
2. Route every non-success push outcome through that probe. Recommended shape: have
   `git_push_to_dev()` raise a distinct "interrupted but verified landed" signal (or return an
   outcome object) rather than `False`/`PushTimeoutError`, so `phase_finish` can mark
   `steps.push.verified_after_failure`, comment, and continue on the success path;
   `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` handles the same signal on its retry.
3. Keep the conservative failure paths unchanged (`open`, manual-push comment, worktree
   retained) with the unknown-outcome wording when the probe returns `None`.
4. Extract the probe so the existing post-*success* ancestry assertion
   `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084, SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U, now completed) reuses it
   rather than shipping a second divergent probe; note the reuse on both items.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` (L5629), `PushTimeoutError` (L4667), `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050), `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011), `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084); new `_verify_commit_on_remote()` helper.
- `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` — the baselines from the test-first slice.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — interrupted-push coverage.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push path.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — the annotation noting the fake must keep resolving a published commit.

## Constraints

- **Positive verification only.** Never report success for a commit that was not observed on `origin/dev`; do not weaken the terminal-status read-back guarantee (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58).
- **No pre-push hook on verification.** The hook runs the full suite (~minutes); verification uses `ls-remote`/`fetch`/`merge-base` only and is bounded (recommended ~60 s). A verification fetch updates only remote-tracking refs, which the live-repo guard already excludes.
- **Ancestry, not equality.** Sibling sessions may push after ours; the commit is landed when it is an *ancestor* of the current `origin/dev` tip. Resolve the short hash from `git_get_commit_hash()` to a full hash before the ancestry check.
- **No force-push, no history rewrite, no `reset --hard`** of the shared main checkout; recovery stays additive.
- **Preserve existing behaviour:** non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry (WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M), worktree retention on genuine failure (WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1), pre-push main-checkout mutation guard, and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics.
- **Report fields are additive.** `steps.push` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (a cleanup test indexes the literal push step); the verified-landed marker is a new optional key, never a renamed or repurposed one.
- **No workflow-language change:** only which outcome (success vs failure) `finish` selects when the remote says the commit landed.
- **Source of truth:** the fix lands in this repository's `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; the installed copy at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` picks it up only after `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared remote-verification probe.** A new `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout) -> bool | None` helper in `implement.py` resolves the full hash (resolving the short hash returned by `git_get_commit_hash()`), reads `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetches that ref when the tip differs (bounded, ~60 s), and returns `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash> <remote-tip>` reports the commit reachable, `False` when positively absent, and `None` when the probe itself failed (network/auth/timeout).
- **Remote-observed verdict before any failure report.** Before `finish` reports a push failure (`PushTimeoutError`, a process-group kill, or a non-zero `git push` exit that is not a non-fast-forward), every non-success outcome is routed through the probe — including the non-fast-forward retry push in `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` — and the verification is time-bounded and uses only ref/object plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite).
- **Verified landed is success, not failure.** When verification confirms the commit is on `origin/dev`, `finish` completes normally: it records the completion comment naming the commit, performs the existing success-path cleanup (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), leaves the work item `completed`/`in_review` (terminal read-back still passes), and marks the report explicitly (`steps.push.verified_after_failure: true` plus the original error text) with an explanatory work-item comment.
- **Genuine failure and unknown outcome stay conservative.** When verification finds the commit absent from `origin/dev`, or verification itself fails (e.g. an `ls-remote` network error), `finish` still fails conservatively: the status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree recovery comment is posted, the worktree is retained, and the message/report distinguishes `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, never claiming success without positive verification.
- **Ancestry, additive fields, preserved behaviour, no duplicate probe.** The commit is considered landed when it is an ancestor of the current `origin/dev` tip, never equality; the probe is extracted so the existing post-success ancestry assertion `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U) reuses it instead of shipping a divergent second probe; non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry, worktree retention on genuine failure, the pre-push main-checkout mutation guard and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics keep working; and `report["steps"]["push"]` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (new keys are additive only).
data.title: Remote-observed push verdict in finish

## Goal

As an operator or implementation agent reading the finish documentation, I want the three push

## Scope
