related-to:SA-0MWJYB95L004LPCZ
target_skill: implement
impact_scope: global
priority_hint: medium
rationale: Push rejection led to stash pop conflicts, checkout/restore attempts, and merge conflicts. A guided recovery path should avoid destructive cleanup and report exact dirty/staged/stash/conflict state.
evidence_sessions: 2026-11-16T14-54-27-990Z_herdr-1794840867-4024106-29197.jsonl

## Summary

Add a read-only recovery diagnosis to `implement.py finish` that reports the exact
repository state and the safe next actions when a push, stash pop or merge goes wrong.

## Problem

A rejected push in the review window led to stash-pop conflicts, `checkout`/`restore`
attempts and merge conflicts, with agents guessing which tree and which stash was
involved. `implement.py` already detects orphaned stashes at `start`, but nothing helps
an agent diagnose a wedged `finish` without reaching for destructive cleanup.

## Users

- AI agents stuck in a failed `finish`: need a diagnosis and a safe, explicit next step.
- Producers: need assurance that recovery never destroys uncommitted work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `implement.py finish` offers a safe git recovery mode that reports dirty, staged, stash and conflict state without destructive cleanup.
  - `finish --recover` reports the resolved repo root, worktree root, branch, upstream, dirty and staged paths, stash entries (with any work-item ids found in them), in-progress merge/rebase/cherry-pick state and conflict paths.
- `--recover` reports dirty, staged, stash and conflict state without destructive cleanup: it exits 0 with the diagnosis and a proposed action list, and never runs `git stash drop`, `git reset --hard`, `git checkout --force` or worktree removal.
- When the pre-push gate or the push fails, `finish` prints the exact `implement.py finish --recover` command for the resolved worktree root instead of leaving the agent to guess.
- Tests assert the diagnosis payload keys and that no destructive git command is ever issued in recovery mode.
- The recovery playbook in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents the mode and its non-destructive guarantee.

## Minimal Implementation

- Tests first: `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_recover_diagnosis.py` (payload keys, conflict/merge-state detection) and `test_finish_recover_never_destructive.py` (command allow-list assertion).
- Add `--recover` to `finish` argument parsing and a diagnosis helper reusing `git_stash_list` and `_extract_work_item_ids_from_stash`, plus existing status/merge-state helpers.
- Wire the push-failure and gate-failure paths to print the recovery command with the resolved root.
- Keep recovery strictly read-only: no commits, no stash mutation, no worktree operations.
- Document the mode, its guarantees and the suggested action order in the two reference docs.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_finish`, `git_stash_list`, `_extract_work_item_ids_from_stash`, `check_orphaned_stashes`, `parse_args`)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_recover_diagnosis.py` (new)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_recover_never_destructive.py` (new)
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `SA-0MWJYSZAP001PCN8` (canonical worktree root): the diagnosis must report the resolved roots rather than re-guess them.

## Risks and assumptions

- Assumption: read-only diagnosis plus an explicit action list is enough to unblock agents; automated repair is out of scope and would violate the never-destructive guarantee.
- Risk: reporting stash entries may expose work from other items on the shared ref; the diagnosis must name ids rather than dump diffs.
- Relationship: the existing orphaned-stash warning at `start` stays as is; this item adds the diagnosis to `finish`.

## Deliverables

- `--recover` diagnosis in `finish` with a non-destructive guarantee and tests.
- Push/gate failure messages that point at the recovery command.

## Impact

A failed push or stash pop stops turning into destructive guesswork: agents see the exact repository state and a safe next step, and uncommitted work survives recovery.

## Summary

Fix `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria()` so section
detection and section exit use one consistent, **heading-level-relative** rule,
and pin it with regression tests written first inside this item (TDD).

Root cause: detection matches any heading level
(`^#+\s+Acceptance\s+Criteria`) but exit breaks only on H2 (`^##\s+`); the later
any-heading branch merely flushes the open entry and continues, so bullets
under a sibling `# Key Files` / `# Related work` heading are collected as ACs
and the coverage review reports them as uncovered.

## Normative rule (agreed with the producer, Option B)

1. Detection captures the AC heading level: `^(#{1,6})\s+Acceptance\s+Criteria`.
2. Inside the section, a heading line `^(#{1,6})\s+` with level **≤** the
   captured level ends the section.
3. A heading **deeper** than the captured level flushes the open AC entry and is
   otherwise ignored (existing behaviour preserved).
4. An unparseable/absent captured level falls back to breaking on level ≤ 2.
5. Fenced code blocks, markdown tables, lone list markers and blank-line
   boundaries are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `extract_acceptance_criteria()` stops collecting AC bullets at the next heading whose level is the same or higher than the AC section heading (levels 1–6), and a deeper heading stays inside the section.
- An H1-headed description whose `# Key Files` and `# Related work` bullets follow `# Acceptance Criteria` returns exactly the AC bullets — no file paths, no related-work entries.
- A `### Acceptance Criteria` section terminated by a sibling `### Key Files` heading stops there, proving the rule is level-relative rather than hard-coded to H1/H2.
- `## Acceptance Criteria` followed by `### Notes` and a bullet still collects that bullet, so `test_heading_inside_ac_section_not_appended` passes unmodified.
- Existing H2-headed parsing tests remain green: `test_stops_at_next_heading`, `test_simple_acs` and the other pre-existing H2 fixtures pass unmodified.
- One test is named for this item's ID (`SA-0MUKCQ4TL0075WZJ`) so the regression is traceable from the suite, and `run_coverage_review` returns `proceed` for an H1-headed parent fixture rather than `stop`.
- The module-level "AC-coverage similarity semantics" docstring, the `extract_acceptance_criteria()` docstring, and the AC-format bullet in `skill/plan/SKILL.md` all describe the same-or-higher termination rule that the code implements.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write the failing regression tests first (H1 sibling leak, H3 section + `### Key Files` sibling, H2 + `### Notes` retained, H2 + `## Constraints` retained, `run_coverage_review` proceeds), then make them pass in the same item so the suite is never left red.
- Capture the AC heading level at detection time; keep it in a local variable alongside `in_ac_section`.
- Replace the `^##\s+` break with a level comparison against the captured level; fold the now-redundant deeper-heading branch into that single check so the function has exactly one heading rule.
- Update the two docstrings and the `skill/plan/SKILL.md` "AC list formats" bullet; do not touch `has_acceptance_criteria_section()` (presence detection is level-agnostic by design).
- No new dependencies; no behaviour change for descriptions whose sections are all H2.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py`
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py`
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md`

## Related work

- child-of: SA-0MUKCQ4TL0075WZJ
- rule-agreed-in: SA-C0MWKJBJUP002RO05 (producer chose Option B)
- absorbed: SA-0MWKJCYJK00430Z8 (a test-only child could not reach a green finish gate; tests and fix are one vertical slice)
- blocks: SA-0MWKJDK8G009ON4T (audit parity)

## Impact

Users planning work items written with H1 or H3 headings no longer see their Key Files paths and related-work links reported as uncovered acceptance criteria.

## Summary

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_extract_acs()` breaks the acceptance
criteria section at **any** heading (`^#{1,6}\s`), which is the opposite of the
rule agreed for `tree_coverage` (stop only at a heading of the same or higher
level than the AC heading). The two extractors therefore disagree on any
description whose AC section contains a deeper sub-heading, even though their
comments claim the audit and plan pipelines "agree on what is an AC section".

Align `_extract_acs()` with the same-or-higher rule and pin the agreement with
a cross-extractor parity test.

## Normative rule (agreed with the producer, Option B)

1. Detection captures the AC heading level (from the markdown heading form; the
   bold / angle-bracket / bare pseudo-heading forms have no level).
2. A markdown heading of level **≤** the captured level ends the section.
3. A **deeper** heading stays inside the section; its bullets are ACs.
4. When the detected heading form carries no level (bold-only, `<<Acceptance>>
   <<criteria>>`, bare `Acceptance Criteria:`), fall back to ending the section
   at level ≤ 2.
5. Checkbox stripping, `*`-bullet acceptance and indented-continuation folding
   are unchanged — only the heading-termination rule moves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A shared fixture whose `## Acceptance Criteria` section contains a `### Notes` sub-heading with a bullet yields the sub-heading bullet as an AC from both `tree_coverage.extract_acceptance_criteria()` and `audit_runner._extract_acs()`.
- The same fixture set produces identical AC lists from both extractors for: an H1-headed description with a `# Key Files` sibling, an H2 section with an H2 sibling, and an H2 section with a deeper H3 sub-heading (fixtures contain no checkboxes and no `*` bullets, so the extractors' other differences do not mask the heading rule).
- `audit_runner._extract_acs()` still stops at an H1 or H2 sibling heading when the AC heading is H1 or H2 respectively, and does not collect `# Key Files` paths.
- An AC section introduced by a level-less pseudo-heading (`**Acceptance criteria:**`, `<<Acceptance>> <<criteria>>`, bare `Acceptance Criteria:`) still ends at an H1 or H2 heading.
- `pytest skill/audit/tests/` and `pytest skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` both pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write the parity test first (red against current `_extract_acs`), reusing the fixture shapes from the sibling tests child rather than re-deriving markdown by hand.
- Capture the heading level in `_extract_acs()` when the matched form is a markdown heading, and compare it on the termination check; default level-less forms to 2.
- Keep the existing `["No acceptance criteria defined."]` fallback and all other parsing untouched.
- Update the comment in `_extract_acs()` that claims alignment with `tree_coverage`, so it states the shared rule rather than a prefix match only.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py`
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py`

## Related work

- child-of: SA-0MUKCQ4TL0075WZJ
- depends-on: SA-0MWKJC810002JFS5 (the shared rule must exist before parity can be pinned)
- evidence: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` line ~7381 (`_MARKDOWN_HEADING_LINE_RE`) and line ~7420 (`if re.match(r"^#{1,6}\s", stripped): break`)

## Impact

Users get the same acceptance-criteria set from a worklog audit as from planning, so a sub-heading inside an AC section can no longer make audit and plan disagree about what the criteria are.

# Implement shared-ref exclusions in git_sandbox

**Parent:** SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH
**Issue type:** bug
**Phase:** 2 — the green implementation for the red tests from the two test children

## Context

The exclusion contract lives once in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`; both guards (`skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` inner plugin and `run_tests.guarded_run_all` outer guard) consume `snapshot_guarded_roots` / `diff_guarded_roots` / `excluded_churn_notes`, so a single constant-level change fixes both and both guarded roots without drift.

Current state: `_is_concurrency_excluded_ref()` matches only `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_EXACT` (`refs/heads/dev`) and `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_NAMESPACES` (`refs/remotes/origin/`, `refs/heads/worklog/`); `NOTED_CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_NAMESPACES` contains only `refs/heads/worklog/`; `excluded_churn_notes()` renders per root with a `where` suffix so a ref shared by both guarded roots would produce two notes.

## Scope

Implement the exclude-and-note remedy for **`refs/stash` only**: the exact ref is excluded from the verdict **and** reported through `EXCLUDED_REF_CHURN_NOTE_PREFIX`, deduplicated to at most one note per movement per run. `refs/notes/*` is deliberately **left monitored** (producer decision 2026-11-17 — stash-only: there is no `git notes` producer in this repo and a notes ref is content, not bookkeeping). No behaviour change for `refs/heads/dev` / `refs/remotes/origin/*` (silent) or `refs/worklog/*` (parser-filtered).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The fix is applied once in the shared helper so both guards (inner `live_repo_guard.py` and outer `guarded_run_all`) and both guarded roots (guarded checkout plus main checkout) benefit without drift, and a shared-ref movement is reported once per run rather than once per guarded root. Verification: code review plus guard-level tests for both consumers.
- `refs/stash` is excluded as an **exact** ref name derived from git plumbing — never a `wl-*`, branch-name or directory-name pattern — and `_is_concurrency_excluded_ref()` returns True for it so `fingerprint()` and `diff_snapshots()` filter the same set and cannot drift. The predicate must **not** match `refs/notes/*` or any other ref (stash-only decision, 2026-11-17).
- `refs/stash` is **noted** as well as excluded: an exact-ref noted companion to `NOTED_CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_NAMESPACES` (or equivalent) makes `_is_noted_concurrency_excluded_ref()` true for it, so the newly excluded shared ref cannot be silently suppressed; `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/*` stay silent and unchanged, and `refs/notes/*` stays monitored and un-noted.
- `excluded_churn_notes()` / `_excluded_ref_churn_notes()` deduplicate a shared ref's movement across guarded roots (one line per ref movement per run) while per-root working-tree attribution notes keep their existing per-checkout naming.
- The existing exclusions (`refs/worklog/*`, `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/*`, `refs/heads/worklog/*`) and the genuine-mutation surfaces (non-excluded refs, local-config keys, clean→dirty working-tree paths) are unchanged.
- The `git_sandbox.py` module docstring states the shared-ref exclusion contract and its accepted blind spot (a suite-caused stash in the guarded root is no longer a ref-level signal).
- Constraints retained: stdlib-only, loadable by file location (`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`), no `sys.path` mutation, no `shared.*`/`test.*` imports, read-only plumbing only (never `gc`, `update-index`, `fetch`, `--refresh`, and never mutate `refs/stash` while probing), no new per-test cost.
- The red tests from the two test children go green, and the existing `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` and `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` suites stay green (changed-scope gate).

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — extend `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_*` / `NOTED_CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_*` constants and the note renderer; update the module docstring.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — consumer; confirm notes reach the run report (no behaviour change expected).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `guarded_run_all` / `_detect_live_repo_mutation` consumer; confirm `live_repo_excluded` notes reach the report (no behaviour change expected).

## Related Work

- Parent SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH; depends on the two test children; precedent SA-0MVV2W9610002CLW (exclude-and-note implementation); contract owners SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65, SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8.

## Summary

Author the failing-first regression tests that pin the desired behaviour: `implement.py start` resumes an item's **existing** worktree and branch even when the work item's current title slug differs from the slug used when the worktree was created (SA-0MVXUHAM3006BRNC AC1–AC4).

New module: `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_slug_drift.py`, following the real-git-repo fixture style of `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py`. `_get_repo_root`, `_discover_worktree`, `worktree_path_for` and `branch_name_for` are deliberately **not** mocked — that mocking is exactly why the sibling defect SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF escaped coverage.

## Why this item comes first

Test-first ordering: these tests are authored before the fix so the fix is provably driven by them. Until the fix lands, the tests are marked `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="SA-0MVXUHAM3006BRNC not fixed yet")`, which keeps the suite green and makes the marker removal in the implementation child a genuine TDD signal (a `strict` xfail fails as soon as the behaviour becomes correct).

## Scenarios

1. **AC1 — resume from the main checkout.** Real temp git repo, canonical worktree and branch created for slug A (`wl-<id>-<slug-a>`); `wl_show` now returns a title whose slug is B; `phase_start` runs from the main checkout. Assert `resumed is True`, `report["worktree_path"]` is the existing tree, `git_worktree_add` is never called, exactly one directory matches `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-*`, and no second branch `wl-<id>-<slug-b>` exists (`git branch --list`).
2. **AC2 — resume from inside the existing worktree.** Same setup with `cwd` = the old-slug worktree; same assertions, plus no `<worktree>/.worklog/worktrees/…` path is created.
3. **AC3 — fresh start unchanged.** No worktree exists and the title is unchanged: `resumed is False`, the tree is created at `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`, branch `wl-<id>-<slug>`.
4. **Already-broken case.** Two worktrees exist for the item (old slug + new slug — the defect's symptom): the tree carrying `.implement_state.json` wins, the run resumes it, and the report names both the chosen and the ignored candidate.
5. **Branch fidelity.** The resumed report's `branch` is the branch actually checked out in the existing worktree, not the slug-derived name.

## Minimal implementation

- Reuse the `_patch_externals`-style context manager pattern from `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py`; hoist a shared helper for "create the worktree for slug X".
- Assert on observable state (report fields, `git branch --list`, directory scan, `git_worktree_add` calls), never on private call shapes.
- Mark the five scenarios `xfail(strict=True)` with the reason string naming this item's fix child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_slug_drift.py` exists and covers scenarios 1–5, each with a real temporary git repository plus a linked worktree (AC4).
- Every test asserts the observable contract — one worktree only, no new branch, and the `resumed` / `worktree_path` / `branch` report fields — rather than internal call shapes.
- The tests do not mock `_get_repo_root`, `_discover_worktree`, `worktree_path_for` or `branch_name_for`.
- With the fix absent, the new module reports the five scenarios as `xfail`ed (never as errors) and the changed-scope suite is green.
- Removing the `xfail` markers on the un-fixed code makes every scenario fail (the test genuinely pins the defect).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_slug_drift.py` (new)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py` (fixture and patch-harness pattern to follow)

## Dependencies

None — created first; the implementation child depends on this one.

## Deliverables

- The regression test module, plus the changed-scope test evidence recorded on this item.

## Impact

The slug-drift defect is pinned by executable tests before the fix, so a title edit can never silently reintroduce a duplicate worktree.

## Summary

Make `implement.py start` resume the item's **existing** worktree (and its existing branch) instead of deriving a fresh path/branch from the work item's current title slug. `phase_start` is the only phase that never consults `_discover_worktree()`; `finish`, `abort`, `parent` and `drive` all do.

## Root cause

`_phase_start_locked` Step 7 computes `worktree_path_for(work_item_id, slug_from_title(title))` and `branch_name_for(...)` from the *current* title and then only checks `_is_worktree()` on that computed path. After a title edit the computed path misses the real tree, `git worktree add -b <new-branch> <new-path> dev` succeeds, and the item ends up with two worktrees (work stranded in the old one while `finish` may remove the emptier new one).

## Minimal implementation

- In `_phase_start_locked` Step 7, when no `--worktree-path` override is given, discover first: reuse `_discover_worktree()` (made repo-root aware so a start from a nested directory of the main checkout still finds the tree) and treat a hit as `resumed`.
- Harden discovery: only accept candidates where `_is_worktree()` is true (`.git` is a **file**), so an abandoned directory left by a failed `git worktree add` is ignored rather than resumed.
- Derive the branch from the discovered worktree itself (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`), falling back to the directory name when detached or unreadable — never from the title slug.
- When several candidates match `wl-<id>-*` (the defect's already-occurred state), pick deterministically: the tree holding `.implement_state.json` first, else the lexicographically first path; log and report the ignored candidates.
- Fall back to today's computed path/branch only when no worktree exists for the item, so a fresh start is byte-identical to current behaviour.
- Surface the decision in the report and the start comment: `slug_drift` (title slug, path slug, branch), the chosen path/branch and any ignored candidates; no duplicate comments.
- Keep `--worktree-path` authoritative with unchanged semantics (absolute as given, relative against `cwd`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** With a worktree already created for slug A and the item title changed to slug B, `implement.py start` from the main checkout resumes the existing worktree (`resumed: true`, `worktree_path` = the existing tree) and never calls `git worktree add`; no second worktree directory and no second `wl-<id>-*` branch are created.
- **AC2:** The same is true when `start` runs from inside the existing (old-slug) worktree.
- **AC3:** When no worktree exists for the item, behaviour is unchanged: the path and branch are derived from the current title slug, `resumed: false`, and the existing `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py` assertions (AC3/AC4) pass unmodified.
- **AC4:** The reported `branch` on a resumed start is the branch actually checked out in the reused worktree, and the report carries `slug_drift` details whenever the title slug differs from the worktree/branch slug.
- **AC5:** Discovery accepts only registered worktrees (`.git` a file) and resolves deterministically when several `wl-<id>-*` directories exist (`.implement_state.json` holder wins), reporting the ignored candidates.
- **AC6:** `--worktree-path` (absolute and relative) keeps its documented precedence and resolution semantics.
- **AC7:** Code comments/docstrings touched by the change explain the resume-before-compute rule and the slug-drift rationale.
- **AC8:** The changed-scope tests pass and the full project suite is green with the change (enforced by the dev-push gate); no existing test is weakened or skipped to accommodate the fix.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_phase_start_locked()` (Step 7), `_discover_worktree()`, `_is_worktree()`, `worktree_path_for()`, `branch_name_for()`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_slug_drift.py` — the regression tests from the prerequisite item (markers removed here).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the regression-test item: the fix lands only after the failing-first tests exist (removing their `xfail` markers is part of this item).

## Deliverables

- The `start` resume fix, green regression tests, and evidence recorded on the work item.

## Impact

Editing a work item's title no longer strands in-progress work in a second, empty worktree — a resumed session always lands back in the tree that already holds its work.

# Goal

As an audit-runner maintainer I want the runner to detect that it is running in a
dispatched / non-interactive context and default child audits to the isolated
`pi` subprocess path, so a herdr-downtime-dispatched audit always finishes its
own child screens instead of leaving them pending for a session that does not exist.

Parent: SA-0MW2J8G260045D17 — Dispatched audits should not emit unservicable screens.
Producer decision (AC1 of the parent): **runner-side** context detection, chosen over a
dispatcher-side `--no-child-in-main-slot` flag because it covers every non-interactive
entry point rather than only the herdr downtime worker.

## Behaviour

- Add a dispatch-detection tier to `_resolve_child_in_main_slot()` in
  `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, consulted **after** the CLI flag and the
  `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` env var and **before** the `True` default.
- The detector reads the dispatch marker env var `HERDR_DOWNTIME` (truthy values
  `1`/`true`/`yes`/`on` → dispatched). Implement it as a small named helper
  (e.g. `_detect_dispatch_context()`) that returns the marker it detected (or `None`)
  so future dispatchers can add markers without restructuring the chain.
- The resolution returns the **source** alongside the value — `flag`, `env`,
  `dispatch-detection`, `default` — so the caller can log it. Keep the existing
  boolean contract working or migrate the single call site deliberately; there is
  exactly one production call site (`_build_audit_context` / `cmd_issue` path,
  `audit_runner.py:17910`).
- Emit exactly one log line at resolution time naming the value and the source,
  e.g. `child_in_main_slot resolved to False (source: dispatch-detection)`. On the
  dispatched path the runner must not emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]`.
- Update `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (the `Child audits in the main LLM slot` section and
  the runner flag list) to document the new tier, the `HERDR_DOWNTIME` marker and the
  documented, actionable state for a dispatched run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The chosen mechanism (runner-side dispatch detection) and the rejected alternative (dispatcher-side flag) are recorded on the parent item with the rationale and the accepted trade-off; this implementation honours that decision and introduces no dispatcher-side `--no-child-in-main-slot` flag anywhere.
- AC2: Dispatched audits no longer emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens that nobody services: a dispatched run completes its child screens itself in isolated `pi` subprocesses.
- AC3: An interactive audit launched from an agent session keeps in-main-slot mode by default — no behaviour change for the interactive path.
- AC4: The resolved mode and its source are logged exactly once at resolution time, naming both the resolved value and the source string (`flag`, `env`, `dispatch-detection`, `default`).
- AC5: `_resolve_child_in_main_slot()` resolves `False` with source `dispatch-detection` when `HERDR_DOWNTIME` is truthy, no CLI flag is passed and `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` is unset.
- AC6: An explicit `--child-in-main-slot` still yields `True` on a dispatched run — the flag keeps absolute precedence over detection.
- AC7: `skill/audit/SKILL.md` documents the new tier, the `HERDR_DOWNTIME` marker, the precedence order and how to override detection.
- AC8: The sibling regression-test item's tests pass and the existing audit-runner test suite still passes.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_child_in_main_slot` (line ~6359), the `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` constant block, the single call site at line ~17910, and `_AuditContext`
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — `Child audits in the main LLM slot` section (~line 226) and the runner flag list (~line 397)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the sibling regression-test item (test-first ordering): the tests encode the contract this item makes pass.
- The `HERDR_DOWNTIME` marker is emitted by the herdr downtime dispatch path, which lives in the **ContentCreator** repository (`packages/ContextHub/packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`). That emission is tracked as a separate cross-repo work item in ContentCreator's own worklog and referenced from the parent; it is **not** editable from this repository's worktree. This item is independently testable without it (the marker is just an input env var).

## Deliverables

- Runner-side dispatch detection with source-tagged resolution, one resolution log line, and updated audit skill documentation.

## Goal

A provider/model-resolution failure at child spawn is retried **inside the same `drive` invocation** on the existing bounded infra-retry budget instead of stopping the chain with `failed_child`.

User story: As an operator running `implement.py drive <epic>`, I want a transient model-routing failure in a child session to be retried automatically, so a healthy child is not abandoned and the chain does not stop.

## Context

`CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) reports five child-session aborts across one drive run (children `CUR-0MWKPMVRH00780TO` ×2, `CUR-0MWKPMWGL005EKZF`, `CUR-0MWKPMX3M0052ZOL` ×2); each child completed on the next `drive` invocation with no code change. This item is **F2** of the upstream plan and depends on **F1** (`classify_spawn_failure` + its tests).

Current behaviour: `phase_drive`'s non-success branch runs `_reconcile_spawn_failure` → `record_spawn_failure` → `_release_orphaned_child_claim` → `report["failed_child"]` + `break`. The existing infra-retry path (`--infra-retry-limit`, `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT = 5`, `_drive_infra_backoff_delay`) covers **only** `finish` refusals and deliberately never spawns a session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After `_reconcile_spawn_failure` reports **non-terminal**, a spawn failure classified `infrastructure` by `classify_spawn_failure` consumes one slot of `--infra-retry-limit` (default 5), sleeps `_drive_infra_backoff_delay(attempt)` and re-spawns the same child within the same invocation — no manual re-run.
- The `children_driven` entry for the retry is `result: "infra-retry"` and carries `step`, `reason`, `attempt` and a `message` naming the provider and model, reusing the additive reporting shape of the finish infra-retry.
- Budget exhaustion produces a chain-stop message naming the provider/model **and an actionable remedy**, instead of a bare `No models match pattern …`; the remedy directive is asserted in a test.
- Ordering is correct and pinned by a test: a child reconciled `completed-late` (already terminal) is **never** retried and no second session is spawned.
- Fail-safe preserved and pinned by a test: an unclassified spawn failure still hard-stops with `report["failed_child"]` and is never retried.
- Retrying does not duplicate side effects: the per-child lock is not re-acquired while held, no second worktree is created, and `record_spawn_failure` evidence is not re-written for an attempt that never produced work.
- The shared budget is documented: `infra_retries[child_id]` is one counter across finish-refusals and spawn retries, and the counter plus `infra_retry_limit` remain present in the drive report.
- Tests use a fake spawner that fails with the provider reason twice and then succeeds on a 5-slot budget, plus the exhaustion, completed-late and unclassified cases (`tests/test_implement_drive.py`, `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`).

## Implementation sketch

1. Extract the retry decision from the finish infra-retry block and call it on the spawn-failure path, **after** reconciliation and before `failed_child`/`break`.
2. Reuse `infra_retries` / `_drive_infra_backoff_delay`; record the `children_driven` entry with the classified provider reason.
3. Re-enter the loop for the same child (`continue`) rather than spawning a different one.

## Constraints

- `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS` stays `(DRIVE_RECURSION_ENV, WORKTREE_ENV, ENV_LOCK_TOKEN)` — no new secrets in argv.
- The commit-preservation gate, `reset-for-retry`, the spawn-failure evidence record (`SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G`), the per-child lock and the terminality reconciliation keep their current semantics; this extends them.
- No session may be spawned for a child that reconciliation proved terminal.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`

## Impact

An operator running a driven epic no longer loses a multi-minute child session — or the whole chain — to an intermittent model-routing error, so a `drive` run becomes self-healing.

## Goal

The implement-skill reference documents the new spawn-time provider-failure recovery path — the infra retry, the `infra-retry` spawn verdict, the release-to-`open` distinction and the configuration remedy — so an operator can diagnose the failure from the docs and the drive report alone.

User story: As an operator whose drive run stopped, I want the reference to tell me what the `children_driven` entry means and what to fix, instead of decoding `No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"`.

## Context

This item is **F5** of the upstream plan for `CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) and depends on **F2** and **F3** (and on the config fold in `SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN`) so the docs describe behaviour that exists.

Existing doc homes to update: the "Drive failure recovery: bounded finish attempts, reconciliation and reset" section (including its verdict table around the `infra-retry` row and the `failed` row) and the "Spawn-failure evidence" section of `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents the spawn-time infrastructure retry: which failures are classified, that it reuses `--infra-retry-limit` and its backoff, and that it re-spawns the same child inside the same invocation.

1. Read the shipped F2/F3 code, then update the two sections and the table rows.
2. Extend `tests/test_implement_docs_drive_recovery.py` with assertions for the new wording/keys.
3. Keep wording consistent with the existing table's vocabulary (`infra-retry`, `failed`, `step`, `reason`, `attempt`).

**Key Files:**
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `tests/test_implement_docs_drive_recovery.py`

An operator reading a stopped drive report can tell a transient provider failure from a real defect and knows the one-line config fix, without reading the drive source.

# Preserve refactor identity markers when intake applies its draft

## Summary

Stop `/skill:intake` from destroying a refactor item's machine-readable identity: before `cmd_finish` applies the intake draft with `wl update --description-file`, carry over every `Refactor-Finding-Key:`, `Refactor-Fingerprint:` and `Refactor-Affected-Lines:` line already in the item's description and place them at the top of the new description. Parent: `SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C` AC1, AC2, AC6.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `intake.py finish <id> --description-file <draft>` writes a description that contains every refactor marker line present in the item's pre-finish description, verbatim, positioned immediately below the draft's leading heading (or at the very top when the draft has no heading).
- Re-running `finish` with the same draft is idempotent: each marker line appears exactly once.
- An item whose description has no marker lines gains none, and an item that is not refactor-created (`Refactor` tag absent and no markers present) is left with the draft applied unchanged.
- Marker extraction only matches the documented marker set at line start (`Refactor-Finding-Key:`, `Refactor-Fingerprint:`, `Refactor-Affected-Lines:`); a marker string quoted mid-line in prose is never treated as a marker.
- The current description is read through the shared `run_wl` helper (worklog-dir resolution respected, caller cwd independent), and a read failure fails closed to "no markers" rather than aborting the intake.
- The applied description is written from a temporary file (no mutation of the caller's draft file), and `finish`'s existing terminal transition (`open` + `intake_complete` + explicit `assignee=""`) and its failure-reset path are unchanged.
- The test module from the sibling test-first item (`skill/intake/tests/test_intake_marker_preservation.py`) passes with no skips.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` § Finish and `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` document marker preservation (what is preserved, why — duplicate suppression, and that nothing is synthesised).
- `python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope changed` (via the test skill) passes.

### Parent AC coverage (parent SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C)

- Parent AC1: Intake `finish` preserves every `Refactor-Finding-Key:`, `Refactor-Fingerprint:` and `Refactor-Affected-Lines:` line present in the item's existing description and places them near the top of the new intake description (the same leading-block convention the refactor skill uses), before the draft is applied.
- Parent AC2: Marker preservation is idempotent and side-effect free: re-running intake does not duplicate marker lines, an item whose description has no markers gains none, and non-refactor items are unchanged.
- Parent AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/intake/SKILL.md`, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Minimal implementation

- Add pure helpers in `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py`: `extract_refactor_markers(text) -> list[str]` (line-start, documented markers only, order preserving, de-duplicated) and `merge_markers_into_draft(draft, markers) -> str` (inserts missing markers below the first leading heading, else at the top; idempotent by construction because only absent lines are inserted).
- In `cmd_finish`, when `description_file` is supplied: `wl show <id> --json` via `run_wl`, extract markers, read the draft, merge, write the merged text to a `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile`/`tmp_path` sibling, then call `_run_wl_update_description(id, merged_path)`.
- Gate preservation on the item being refactor-created: `Refactor` tag present in the `wl show` payload **or** at least one marker already present; otherwise apply the draft untouched.
- Keep `_run_wl_update_description` unchanged apart from accepting the merged path; extend its docstring to record the marker contract.

## Key Files

- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — marker extraction/merge helpers and the `cmd_finish` wiring.
- `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_marker_preservation.py` — the contract written by the test-first sibling.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — § Finish step documentation.
- `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` — maintainer reference section on marker preservation.

## Constraints

- Do not change the refactor marker format or identity semantics.
- Never synthesise or resurrect markers; preserve only what exists.
- No `wl` schema change, no bulk data migration.
- Follow the shared status-lifecycle and assignee-release invariants (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`); the explicit `assignee=""` releases must stay explicit.
- Validate through the test skill / changed-scope gate; no ad-hoc test runs.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the test-first contract item (marker preservation tests).

## Deliverables

- Working preservation path in `intake.py` plus updated intake documentation.

# Add a legacy identity fallback to the refactor duplicate guard

## Summary

Make the refactor pre-creation duplicate guard see items that lost their identity markers, so an intake-rewritten refactor item still suppresses a repeat filing. When `_find_existing_worklog_item()` finds no `Refactor-Finding-Key:` for a candidate item, reconstruct `<code>:<repository-relative path>` from its title/description and compare it exactly. Parent: `SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C` AC3, AC4, AC6.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_find_existing_worklog_item()` consults the whole refactor family, not only marker-carrying items: after the existing `wl list "Refactor-Finding-Key:"` lookup it performs one `wl list --tags Refactor --json` lookup for legacy candidates (a marker-only query can never return a marker-less item).
- For a candidate with no `Refactor-Finding-Key:` marker the guard reconstructs the identity from, in order: structured `- **Code:**` / `- **File:**` description fields, the `## Code Smell:` heading plus `- **File:**`, and the `Refactor: <smell> in <path>` title (path from the title's `in <path>` suffix, code from the recorded rule/smell). The reconstructed identity is normalised and compared **exactly** with the smell's identity — no substring matching anywhere.
- Both halves must be established for a match; when either the code or the path cannot be determined the candidate is a non-match (fail open — a genuinely new finding is still filed).
- A marker-carrying item is always matched via its marker; the legacy reconstruction is only a fallback, and its result never overrides or contradicts a parsed marker.
- Terminal (`completed` / `deleted`) legacy items remain non-matches, and a legacy item whose reconstructed path differs from, or merely contains, the target path (`skill/x.py.bak` vs `skill/x.py`) never matches.
- The legacy parsing is **shared** with `skill/refactor/scripts/consolidate_duplicates.py` (extract the field/title parsing into one helper in `workitem_creation.py` and have the consolidation tool import it, or an equivalently single-source arrangement) so the two cannot drift; `tests/test_refactor/test_consolidate_duplicates.py` keeps passing unchanged.
- The legacy lookup is best-effort: a failing or slow `wl` call logs and returns "no legacy match" rather than raising, preserving the guard's existing fail-open behaviour.
- The contract tests from the sibling test-first item (`tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py` legacy-fallback section) pass with no skips.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` § Finding identity and dedupe and `docs/refactor.md` § 4 (Work Item Creation for Pre-existing Smells) document the legacy fallback (when it applies, exactness, fail-open, and that legacy items are matched but never rewritten to add markers).
- `python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope changed` (via the test skill) passes.

### Parent AC coverage (parent SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C)

- Parent AC3: The refactor pre-creation duplicate guard (`_find_existing_worklog_item`) matches a non-terminal marker-less legacy item by reconstructing its `<code>:<repository-relative path>` identity from the item's title/description (structured `- **Code:**` plus `- **File:**` fields, or the `Refactor: <smell> in <path>` title plus the recorded rule), using exact normalised comparison and no substring matching, so items already damaged by an earlier intake rewrite do not breed duplicates.
- Parent AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/intake/SKILL.md`, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Minimal implementation

- In `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py`, add a shared pure parser `parse_legacy_item_identity(item) -> str | None` returning a raw `<code>:<path>` (or `{code, path}`) from the legacy structured fields/title; name and document the three-source precedence.
- Add `_find_legacy_worklog_item(smell, repo_root)` mirroring `_find_existing_audit_twin`'s shape (subprocess `wl list --tags Refactor --json`, 15 s timeout, "fail open" on any error), skipping items that carry a marker and terminal items, and matching on normalised exact identity.
- Call it from `_find_existing_worklog_item` after the marker loop, before returning `None`; keep the repeat-comment / line-union behaviour in `create_smell_work_item` working for a legacy match (a legacy item's `Refactor-Affected-Lines` may be absent — an appended repeat comment is still correct, a silent dedupe must not crash on an empty tracked line set).
- Update `skill/refactor/scripts/consolidate_duplicates.py::_item_identity` to delegate to the shared parser, keeping its main-root path normalisation.
- Update the module docstring/`__all__`-style documentation list in `workitem_creation.py` and the refactor SKILL.md section.

## Key Files

- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — shared legacy parser plus `_find_existing_worklog_item` / new `_find_legacy_worklog_item`.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/consolidate_duplicates.py` — delegate legacy parsing to the shared helper.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py` — the contract written by the test-first sibling.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_consolidate_duplicates.py` — must keep passing.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — duplicate-prevention documentation.
- `docs/refactor.md` — user-facing § 4 work-item-creation documentation.

## Constraints

- Do not change the marker format or identity semantics (`<code>:<repository-relative path>`, line excluded).
- Never rewrite a legacy item to add markers — matching is read-only.
- No `wl` schema change, no bulk migration; the historical duplicates stay the consolidation tool's job.
- Do not widen the lookup into non-refactor items (tag-gated), so an unrelated description mentioning a file path cannot suppress a real finding.
- Validate through the test skill / changed-scope gate; no ad-hoc test runs.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the legacy-fallback test-first contract item.

## Deliverables

- Legacy identity fallback in the duplicate guard, shared parser, and updated refactor documentation.

# End-to-end regression: intake-rewritten refactor item suppresses a repeat filing

## Summary

Prove the two halves join up: after `/skill:intake` has rewritten a refactor item's description (marker preserved by half 1, or already lost on a legacy item and recovered by half 2), the next refactor scan files **no** duplicate. Parent: `SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C` AC5, AC7.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An integration test drives the real intake `finish` path (draft file → `cmd_finish`) against a refactor item that carries all three markers, then feeds the resulting description into the refactor duplicate guard and asserts the guard returns that item instead of creating a new one.
- A second integration case covers the pre-damaged legacy item: a description with no markers (intake-style prose plus `- **Code:**` / `- **File:**` or a `Refactor: <smell> in <path>` title) is recognised by the guard through the legacy fallback.
- A control case proves no over-suppression: the same flow with a *different* rule code files a new item; a terminal legacy item does not suppress.

# Audit code-quality scan lints gitignored paths (explicit scope bypasses `.gitignore`)

## Problem

The audit's automated code-quality scan files lint findings against files the
project's `.gitignore` excludes — notably `.worklog/` scratch scripts and
worktree copies — even though no committable remediation exists for them. The
2026-10-29 llm-project reviews produced exactly this: three items filed against
`.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` (one `critical` F401, one `high` E401,
one `medium` I001), each of which could only be closed as a verification-only
no-op.

Impact: scheduling noise in every audited project, and a `critical`-tagged
phantom competes with real defects in `wl next`. Worse, the loop is
self-sustaining — a filed child repeats the offending path in its
description/`Key Files`, which re-enters the item-derived scan scope on the next
audit.

## Root cause (verified, not assumed)

1. `_resolve_code_quality_scope` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`)
   resolves an **explicit file scope**: first the git changed-file list
   (`git diff --name-only HEAD` + `git status --porcelain=v1`), then the item's
   committed touched files / `Key Files` (`_resolve_touched_files`).
2. `_filter_code_quality_scope` bounds that scope by project containment and
   nested repositories only (SA-0MVPDTSRV0049KW2). It applies **no `.gitignore`
   check** — there is no `git check-ignore` anywhere in `skill/audit/scripts/`
   or `skill/code_review/scripts/`.
3. `run_ruff` (`skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py`, `_run_ruff_check`)
   therefore receives the gitignored path **as an explicit argument**, and ruff
   lints explicitly-passed paths regardless of `.gitignore`, even with
   `--force-exclude`. Probe (2026-11-18, `~/projects/llm`, repo `.venv` ruff),
   against a scratch file under the gitignored `.worklog/analysis/`:

   - `git check-ignore -v` → `.gitignore:6:.worklog/`
   - `ruff check <path> --extend-exclude '**/*.ts,**/*.yaml' --force-exclude --output-format json`
     → **3 findings** (F401 ×2, I001) — the audit's command shape
   - `ruff check .worklog/analysis/` (directory recursion) → `All checks passed!`

   So only the explicit-path scope is defective; ruff's own traversal already
   honours `.gitignore`.

A gitignore-aware filter already exists: `refactor.path_filters.filter_scannable_paths`
(default `.worklog` exclusion plus a batched `git check-ignore --no-index`).
Probe: `filter_scannable_paths(['.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py',
'proxy/server.py'], repo_root='~/projects/llm')` → `['proxy/server.py']`.

## Acceptance Criteria

Test-first: AC1–AC5 are pinned by failing tests written before the fix.

1. `_filter_code_quality_scope` drops any path matched by the project's
   `.gitignore`, for **both** scope sources (git changed-file list and
   item-derived touched/`Key Files`). Verified by a unit test on a temporary git
   repository whose `.gitignore` excludes a directory that holds a `.py` file.
2. A tracked-but-gitignored file is dropped too (the `--no-index` case), while a
   tracked in-scope file in the same list is retained — no over-filtering.
3. A merely **untracked but not ignored** file is retained, because an audit of
   in-progress work must still lint the item's brand-new files.
4. Gitignore filtering uses **one batched** `git check-ignore` call (no
   per-file subprocess) and degrades gracefully — on git failure / non-repository
   root the paths are kept and a warning is logged, so a git problem never
   silently empties the audit's lint scope.
5. Existing scope behaviour is preserved: containment inside the project root,
   nested-repository exclusion, the dropped-paths stderr warning, input order,
   and the `_FILE_SCOPE_MAX_FILES` cap.
6. The helper is **reused**, not reimplemented: the audit calls
   `refactor.path_filters.filter_scannable_paths` (or its batched
   `git check-ignore` core) rather than adding a second gitignore
   implementation.
7. A gitignored-path finding is never filed: with the scope fixed, a scan of
   `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` in `~/projects/llm` emits zero
   findings — recorded as command + output on this item (no severity demotion
   path is added; the scope filter is the single gate).
8. `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` documents the code-quality scan-scope
   contract (project containment → nested repository → `.gitignore`) as the
   documented scope assertion, and the `_run_ruff_check` docstring records that
   `--force-exclude` does **not** cover explicitly-passed gitignored paths.
9. The audit and code-review suites pass via the test skill, plus the full suite
   at the dev-push gate.

## Implementation sketch

1. Write the red tests first in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_code_quality_scope.py`
   (tmp git repo + `git init`, in the style of the existing containment tests).
2. Extend `_filter_code_quality_scope` to run the surviving paths through
   `refactor.path_filters.filter_scannable_paths` (with
   `require_source_extension=False`, preserving the existing `.py`-narrowing in
   `_run_ruff_check`) before applying the nested-repository/containment bounds;
   keep the dropped-count stderr warning and extend its message to distinguish
   gitignored drops.
3. Re-run the probe scan against `~/projects/llm/.worklog/analysis/` and paste
   the result on this item (AC7 evidence).
4. Update `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and the `_run_ruff_check`
   docstring (AC8).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_filter_code_quality_scope` (fix
  site), `_resolve_code_quality_scope`, `_resolve_touched_files`.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_code_quality_scope.py` — regression tests.
- `skill/refactor/path_filters.py` — reused batched
  `git check-ignore --no-index` filtering.
- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — ruff invocation docstring (the
  `--force-exclude` limitation).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — documented scan-scope contract.

## Constraints

- No new third-party dependency; no new gitignore implementation.
- One batched git call; graceful degradation when git is unavailable.
- Merely untracked files must stay in scope (audits of in-progress work).
- No behaviour change beyond the gitignore exclusion.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the historical trigger for the 2026-10-29 findings could not be
  fully reconstructed from the log; the defect is reproducible on the current
  tree with the probe above, so the fix is justified regardless.
- **Risk:** an over-broad filter silently shrinks audit coverage — pinned by
  AC2/AC3 (tracked and untracked-not-ignored files retained).
- **Risk:** a cross-skill import (audit → refactor). Accepted by the producer
  (Q3 answer (a)); extraction into `skill/shared/` is the follow-up if a third
  caller appears.
- **Assumption (documented):** priority raised from the relocated item's `low` to
  `medium` because the defect files `critical`-severity noise in every audited
  project and self-perpetuates across items.

## Provenance

Relocated from the llm-project item `LP-0MVTKJ8KN0069TJV` (producer decision
2026-11-18, Q1 answer (a)): the defect lives in this repository's agent
infrastructure, so it is implemented and released here; the llm item is deleted
after relocation. Discovered while no-op-closing `LP-0MVTJXCN7000V3SA` (F401 on
`.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1:** "Where should the fix be implemented — a SorraAgents work item
  (relocate), or directly from the llm item with explicit permission to edit
  `skill/`?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-18):** Relocate; delete the llm item
  after relocation, and `wl sync` once this item is created. Final: relocate.
- **Q2:** "For a gitignored-path finding that still reaches the quality-epic
  filer, should nothing be filed, should it be filed `low` with an 'untracked
  scratch file' note, or both?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-18):** (a) — file
  nothing; the scope filter is the only gate (AC7). Final: (a).
- **Q3:** "May the audit reuse `refactor.path_filters.filter_scannable_paths`,
  extract the batched `git check-ignore` core into `skill/shared/`, or duplicate
  a minimal check?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-18):** (a) — reuse. Final:
  (a) (AC6).
- **Q4 (agent research):** "Does ruff already honour `.gitignore` for the
  explicit-path scope the audit uses?" — **Answer (probe 2026-11-18,
  `~/projects/llm`):** No; directory recursion passes, an explicitly-passed
  gitignored `.py` file still yields F401/I001 findings with `--force-exclude`.
- **Q5 (agent research):** "Is a gitignore-aware scan filter already available?"
  — **Answer (probe of `skill/refactor/path_filters.py`):** Yes; it drops
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` and keeps `proxy/server.py`.
- **Q6 (agent research):** "Is this already covered by an existing item?" —
  **Answer (`wl search`, both stores):** No; `SA-0MVPDVXT90067E3M` fixed the
  refactor skill's scan scope but not the audit's code-quality scope.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-18 — created by the plan skill as the relocation target for
  `LP-0MVTKJ8KN0069TJV` (producer Q1 (a)). Root cause verified by probe;
  features F1–F3 (tests → scope-filter fix → end-to-end verification + docs)
  form one vertical slice, so no child work items are needed. F4 (severity
  demotion at filing time) was dropped per producer Q2 (a).

data.description:
# Problem

`implement.py parent` / `implement.py drive` fail closed **before any session is
spawned** when the repository already holds ambient uncommitted work in the main
checkout or in other items' registered worktrees.
`_child_main_checkout_violation()` attributes that pre-existing dirt to a
never-spawned child whose own worktree is clean (zero commits ahead of `dev`),
because its "any other change surface holds changes" condition has no time
component. The only current exemption is the spawn-failure record, which exists
only after the driver has attempted a spawn and the session died
(SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G) — it cannot apply to a child that will be spawned by the
very same `phase_parent` call.

Reproduction (2026-11-17, `llm` epic `LP-0MVVCO1N7004TNGY`): a dirty main
checkout plus four dirty sibling worktrees plus a startable child with an
existing clean worktree ⇒ `drive` spawns **0** sessions and reports every dirty
surface as the child's stray write.

# User story

As an operator driving an epic, I want `implement.py drive <epic>` to start the
next startable child even when the repository already holds unrelated
uncommitted work, so that a long-lived checkout with several items in flight
does not make every epic undriveable.

# Acceptance Criteria

- A regression test builds the incident shape over real git sandboxes (`shared.git_sandbox`): ≥1 dirty tracked path in the main checkout, ≥1 dirty registered sibling worktree, and a startable (`open`) child with an existing clean worktree holding zero commits ahead of `dev`; `phase_parent` reports the child startable (`next_child` set, implementation action) with `placement_violation` not True and `success` True.
- A regression test asserts `phase_drive` spawns the next startable child in that scenario through an injected fake `spawn_session` (no real Pi session), and its report does not name any unrelated sibling worktree as an offender.
- A regression test asserts the genuine case still fails closed: a child whose session baseline predates the write and which writes only into the main checkout — or only into another item's linked worktree — is still reported as `placement_violation: True` even when other pre-existing dirt is present.
- Existing sibling-stray detection tests in `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` are updated to establish a session baseline before the injected write, and all continue to pass.
- The regression tests are written first (TDD) and land green. `implement.py finish` refuses a red tree, so they ship in the same commit as the fix children (mirroring SA-0MWGZ8E7C001X2HA / SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G).
- Full suite green at the dev-push gate (parent AC5) — the new regression tests and the existing suite pass together.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — incident reproduction, drive-spawn assertion, genuine-stray preservation.

# Tests

1. Never-spawned child + dirty main checkout + dirty sibling worktrees ⇒ `phase_parent` reports startable, no violation (parent AC1).
2. `phase_drive` in that scenario spawns exactly one child session via the fake spawner and names no sibling as an offender (parent AC3).
3. Session-baselined child writes only into the main checkout ⇒ still a placement violation (parent AC2).
4. Session-baselined child writes only into a sibling worktree ⇒ still a placement violation (parent AC2).

# Impact

A driver can start the next child of an epic on a checkout that already holds other items' uncommitted work, instead of every epic becoming undriveable until that dirt is cleaned.

data.description:
# Problem

`_child_main_checkout_violation()` has no notion of time: it treats **any**
dirty foreign surface (the main checkout or a registered sibling worktree) as
evidence that the child wrote outside its worktree. A reusable snapshot
primitive and a snapshot-aware comparison let the guard distinguish
pre-existing/ambient dirt from a write that happened during the child's
session.

This is the core fix child (parent AC1/AC2/AC4 mechanics). It adds the
primitive and makes the guard baseline-aware **without** changing behaviour when
no baseline is supplied, so existing callers and tests keep working until the
lifecycle child (sibling item) wires the baseline through.

# User story

As an `implement.py` maintainer, I want the placement guard to compare foreign
change surfaces against a recorded baseline, so that only writes attributable to
the child fail the chain closed.

# Acceptance Criteria

- `_snapshot_foreign_surfaces(repo_root, child_worktree, parent_branch=...)` returns a deterministic, sorted mapping `{surface_abs_path: {"dirty": [repo-relative paths], "head": "<sha>"}}` covering the main checkout and every path returned by `_registered_sibling_worktree_paths`, excluding `.worklog/` paths and project-declared expected-dirty paths.
- A comparison helper (e.g. `_foreign_surface_offenders_since(baseline)`) returns, per surface, only the dirty paths that are new or whose status changed since the baseline, plus surfaces whose HEAD moved (commits ahead added since the baseline).
- `_child_main_checkout_violation()` accepts an optional baseline (plus a loader for the persisted record); when a baseline is supplied it reports a violation only for surfaces/paths new or changed since the baseline and returns `None` when nothing changed. With no baseline it keeps the current full-guard behaviour, so no existing caller or test regresses.
- The violation message for a genuine post-baseline write still names the offending paths, the offending sibling root(s) and the child's own worktree (parent AC4).
- Unit tests over real git sandboxes cover: clean baseline ⇒ no violation; dirt present in the baseline ⇒ no violation; a new dirty path after the baseline ⇒ violation naming only that path; a sibling worktree whose HEAD advanced after the baseline ⇒ violation.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_snapshot_foreign_surfaces`, the comparison helper, `_child_main_checkout_violation`, `_registered_sibling_worktree_paths`, `_main_checkout_offending_paths`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — guard-level unit coverage.

# Tests

1. Clean baseline, clean surfaces ⇒ no violation.
2. Baseline includes the ambient dirt, surfaces unchanged ⇒ no violation.
3. Baseline recorded, then a new main-checkout path written ⇒ violation naming only the new path.
4. Baseline recorded, then a sibling worktree gains a commit ahead of `dev` ⇒ violation naming the sibling root.
5. No baseline supplied ⇒ legacy full-guard behaviour unchanged (existing tests).

# Impact

The placement guard stops blaming a child for dirt that already existed when its session context was established, while still catching every genuine post-baseline write.
data.title: Fix: snapshot-aware placement guard primitive

data.description:
# Problem

The snapshot primitive is only useful if a baseline is recorded **before** a
child's session can write and read back afterwards. Wire the baseline through
the `start` → `parent` → `drive` lifecycle and persist it under the child's
`.worklog/`, mirroring the durable spawn-failure record
(`<worktree>/.worklog/spawn-failure.json`, SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G).

This child completes parent AC1 and AC3 end to end: a never-spawned child is
exempt (no session has run), and a spawned child's writes are attributable on
the next `parent` pass.

# User story

As an operator driving an epic, I want the driver to record where the repository
stood before each child session and to re-read that record afterwards, so that
only a session's own writes fail the chain.

# Acceptance Criteria

- `phase_start` records a session baseline for the child in `<worktree>/.worklog/` (a path every dirty-path helper excludes) before any session runs; the record disappears with the worktree.
- `phase_drive` refreshes the child's session baseline immediately **before** spawning each child session, so a session's writes are attributable on the next `phase_parent` pass.
- `phase_parent` supplies the persisted baseline to `_child_main_checkout_violation` at both call sites (the `skip-in-progress` path and the `implement` path); when no baseline exists it records an ambient one before checking, so pre-existing dirt is never attributed to a never-spawned child.
- The baseline record never counts as work: `_classify_child_worktree` still reports `CHILD_CLEAN` and `_has_worktree_changes` stays False after it is written.
- A missing, malformed, or foreign-child baseline fails open to the legacy guard (never silently exempts a child).
- Tests cover the drive spawn boundary (baseline written before a fake spawn and read by the next parent pass), the never-spawned exemption, and the `.worklog/` exclusion.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_start`, `phase_drive`, `phase_parent`, `record_session_baseline` / `read_session_baseline` (new helpers), `SPAWN_FAILURE_FILE` precedent.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — lifecycle coverage.

# Tests

1. `phase_start` writes a baseline under `.worklog/`; the child stays `CHILD_CLEAN`.
2. `phase_drive` refreshes the baseline before the fake spawn; the next `phase_parent` sees a post-baseline write as a violation.
3. A never-spawned child with ambient dirt and no baseline records an ambient baseline and is reported startable (parent AC1).
4. An unreadable/foreign baseline falls back to the legacy guard.

# Impact

`drive` can hand off the next child of an epic on a checkout with unrelated in-flight work, and still fails closed the moment a spawned session writes outside its own worktree.
data.title: Fix: session-baseline lifecycle across start/parent/drive

data.description:
# Problem

The placement-guard documentation and the implement skill reference describe the
guard only in terms of "a foreign change surface holds changes", with the
spawn-failure record as the sole exemption. They do not document the
baseline/threshold semantics that make pre-existing ambient dirt exempt, so an
operator reading the docs would still expect the guard to fire for unrelated
in-flight work.

# User story

As an `implement.py` maintainer or operator, I want the placement guard's
baseline semantics documented, so I can predict when ambient dirt is exempt and
when a genuine stray write still fails closed.

# Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (The placement guard section) documents that pre-existing/ambient dirt in the main checkout and in registered sibling worktrees is **not** a placement violation, and explains the baseline/threshold semantics (what is captured, when it is captured/refreshed, and what counts as a post-baseline write).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents the same semantics for `_child_main_checkout_violation`, `phase_start`, `phase_parent` and `phase_drive`, including where the baseline record lives under `.worklog/`.
- The docs state that a genuine post-baseline write still fails closed and names the offending paths and the child's own worktree.
- The docs keep the existing spawn-failure exemption description consistent with the new baseline mechanism (no contradictory rules).

**Key Files:**
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — The placement guard section.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — spawn-failure evidence section and the `_child_main_checkout_violation` reference.

# Tests

- Documentation-only change; verified by the docs lint/tests that cover these files (no new behavioural tests).

# Impact

Operators and maintainers can predict when pre-existing in-flight work is exempt from the placement guard and can debug a refusal from the docs alone.

# Pre-commit hook guard sandbox tests

## Goal

As the implementer of the commit-time guard, I want a hermetic test that pins
exactly when `.githooks/pre-commit` must refuse and when it must stay silent, so
the guard can never regress into blocking legitimate work.

Test-first half of parent AC3. This item writes **tests only** — the hook itself
is the sibling item *Pre-commit hook refuses main-checkout dev commits*.

## Context

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` is the sanctioned sandbox: `fixture_git_env()`,
  `scrub_repository_overrides()`, `run_git()`. It strips inherited `GIT_*`
  overrides so a polluted session environment cannot leak into the fixture.
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` is the precedent for a throw-away repo
  built from the committed `.githooks/` with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` is the precedent for asserting the
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` wiring block itself.
- The guard target is narrow: **`dev` in the main checkout**. A linked worktree,
  a feature branch, `git merge --ff-only` and a `wl sync` commit must all pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new hermetic module `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py` builds a
  throw-away repository from the committed `.githooks/` with
  `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a bare local `origin` and a sandboxed `$HOME`; it
  never touches the real checkout, the real `$HOME` or the network.
- It asserts a commit on `dev` in the main checkout is **refused at commit time**:
  non-zero exit, `HEAD` unchanged, no new commit object, and the refusal message
  names the branch (`dev`), the main checkout path, the worktree requirement and
  the operator override.
- Zero-width proof: after the refused commit attempt the repository's commit
  count and `git rev-parse HEAD` are byte-identical to the pre-attempt values.
- It asserts the hook does **not** fire (exit 0, commit created) when:
  (a) the same commit runs inside a linked worktree (`git worktree add`);
  (b) the main checkout is on a feature branch;
  (c) `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1` is set (and the override announces
  itself on stderr so a deliberate hot-fix stays auditable).
- It asserts the two legitimate main-checkout movements still succeed: a
  `git merge --ff-only` fast-forward of `dev` (no commit object is created) and a
  `wl sync`-style commit performed inside a temporary linked worktree
  (`.worklog/tmp-worktree-*`, detached `HEAD`) — the shape
  `ContextHub/dist/sync/worktree.js::withTempWorktree` uses.
- The suite is environment-clean: the fixture uses `fixture_git_env()` /
  `scrub_repository_overrides()` so inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` or
  `GIT_WORK_TREE` cannot influence a verdict.
- Tests are run only through the test skill (`run_tests.py`), never ad hoc; the
  new module passes once the hook item lands, and is red before it (the hook
  does not exist yet).

## Minimal implementation

- One test module, module-level docstring citing parent AC3 and the four
  negative cases, helper functions for "make a repo", "commit a file", "add a
  linked worktree".
- No production code, no changes to `.githooks/`, no changes to
  `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` (pattern to reuse)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before *Pre-commit hook refuses main-checkout dev commits*.

## Deliverables

- The failing-first test module and a short note on the red→green transition.

# Commit-helper guard tests for audit and code-review

## Goal

As a producer, I want the three skill commit helpers pinned by hermetic tests, so
"refuse to commit on `dev` in the main checkout" cannot be silently dropped from
one of them — especially from the duplicate `skill/code_review/` directory.

Test-first half of parent AC1. Tests only; the hardening is the sibling items
*Shared main-checkout commit guard + audit hardening* and *Harden code-review
commit helper in both directories*.

## Context

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_commit_config_remediation` (≈14222)
  stages one config file and commits with `REMEDIATION_COMMIT_MESSAGE`, locally,
  no push. Returns the short sha or `None`; its call site (≈14439) records
  failures into `results["chore_failures"]`.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (≈425) and the
  duplicate `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` (≈641) run `git add .`
  + `git commit -m "Auto-fix: <linter> applied fixes"`. Both directories are
  live: `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` and
  `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` import `code_review`; `code-review` is
  the skill-facing package that owns `SKILL.md`.
- The shared detection verdict must agree with `.githooks/pre-commit`:
  main checkout ⟺ `git rev-parse --git-dir` == `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`;
  target branch ⟺ `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` == `dev`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hermetic tests (built on `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`) cover
  `_commit_config_remediation` and `_commit_changes` in both code-review
  directories.
- Refusal case: on `dev` in the main checkout the helper makes **no commit** and
  leaves **no staged change** behind (the staging step never runs), and returns
  its failure sentinel (`None` / `False`).
- Positive cases preserved: in a linked worktree, and on a feature branch in the
  main checkout, each helper still commits a real change — pinned for both.
- `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1` makes every helper commit (consistent with
  the hook), and the override is logged so the deliberate act is traceable.
- Audit call site: a refusal is recorded in `results["chore_failures"]` with a
  message naming the worktree requirement and the work-item id, so the audit
  report states why the remediation was not committed — it is never silently
  dropped.
- The two code-review helper twins are parametrised in one test so they cannot
  drift apart again; an explicit assertion pins "both directories refuse
  identically".
- Unit tests for the new `skill/shared/commit_guard.py` detection helper
  (`is_main_checkout`, `current_branch`, `commit_refusal_reason`) cover the
  main-checkout, linked-worktree, feature-branch, detached-`HEAD` and override
  cases — so a shell and a Python verdict can never disagree.

## Minimal implementation

- One audit test module, one parametrised code-review test module, and one
  helper-unit test module (or a single module with three test classes).
- No production-code edits.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/` (new module for `_commit_config_remediation`)
- `skill/code-review/tests/` and/or `skill/code_review/tests/` (new parametrised module)
- `skill/shared/tests/` (new `test_commit_guard.py`)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before the two hardening items.

## Deliverables

- Red-first tests for all three helpers plus the shared guard primitive.

# Start refusal attribution tests

## Goal

As a producer, when `implement.py start` refuses because `dev` is not a pushed
tip, I want the refusal pinned by tests that name the owning work items, so
reconciliation is one step instead of a manual log trawl.

Test-first half of parent AC2. Tests only; the implementation is the sibling item
*Start refusal names owning work items*.

## Context

- `_resolve_start_base` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` ≈8021) produces
  `reason: local_dev_not_a_pushed_tip` and an opaque three-step warning
  (≈8123-8137). `phase_start` (≈12081-12110) posts a work-item comment naming
  only the two tips, then releases the claim to `open`.
- `WORK_ITEM_ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}-[A-Z0-9]{2,})\b")` at
  `implement.py` ≈1951 is the existing id pattern — reuse it, do not add a
  second one.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_start_base_resolution.py` already has
  `test_base_refuses_local_dev_with_unpushed_commits` (≈112) and
  `test_phase_start_refuses_a_worktree_from_unpushed_local_dev` (≈315); extend
  that module rather than starting a new one.
- Related work: SA-0MVY4SG8O001RSQF (open) establishes that commit **body**
  mentions are not ownership evidence — AC2 says *subject scan*, so ownership is
  resolved from the subject only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `skill/implement/tests/test_start_base_resolution.py` gains tests asserting the
  refusal names the owning work item(s) for commits whose **subject** contains an
  id (e.g. `fix: Wrap implicit string concatenation (SA-0MWDKRD8G008Z164)`).
- A commit with no id in its subject is reported as **unattributed** — never
  dropped and never silently attributed to the current work item.
- An id present only in the commit **body** does not make that item the owner
  (subject-scan-only contract, consistent with SA-0MVY4SG8O001RSQF).
- The report carries the attribution machine-readably (per-commit sha, subject,
  owning ids and an `unattributed` flag) under
  `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]`, so `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` and
  future tooling do not have to re-parse prose.
- The `phase_start` work-item comment names the owning items, keeps the existing
  three-step remedy (inspect, verify, push or reset with operator confirmation)
  and points at the reconciliation helper.
- The refusal decision itself is unchanged: `worktree_refused is True`, no
  worktree created, claim released to `open` — the pushed-tip invariant stays
  exactly as it is.
- Fail-open coverage: an unreachable remote (fetch failure) still branches from
  local `dev`; attribution absence never turns a legitimate start into a refusal.
- Message bound: a long unpushed range is truncated with an explicit
  "… and N more" so the warning stays readable, and that truncation is tested.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend the existing module with attribution-specific tests and a helper that
  builds a repo with 3 unpushed commits (attributed, unattributed, body-only id).
- No production-code edits.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_start_base_resolution.py` (extend)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before *Start refusal names owning work items*.

## Deliverables

- Red-first attribution tests.
