# Reconcile unpushed dev helper tests

## Goal

As a producer, I want the reconciliation helper's contract pinned by tests —
push by default, reset only on explicit confirmation — so recovery from a
poisoned `dev` can never destroy work by accident.

Test-first half of parent AC4. Tests only; the script and its documentation are
the sibling item *Reconcile unpushed dev helper script and docs*.

## Context

- The helper will live at `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` and is documented
  in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (pushed-tip guarantees section,
  ≈2638).
- Existing precedents for testing a repository script hermetically:
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`, `tests/test_cleanup_scripts.py`, and
  the sandbox helpers in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`.
- Push policy: pushes go to `dev` only — never `main`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `tests/test_reconcile_unpushed_dev.py` builds a bare local `origin` plus
  a clone whose `dev` carries unpushed commits; no real checkout, `$HOME` or
  network is touched.
- Listing: output names each `origin/dev..dev` commit (short sha + subject) and
  its owning work item(s) parsed from the subject, with an explicit
  **unattributed** bucket.
- Default action is **push**: after a plain run, `origin/dev` advanced and local
  `dev` equals `origin/dev`.
- Reset is opt-in only: without the explicit confirmation flag the helper refuses,
  mutates nothing (both refs byte-identical) and names the flag; with it, the
  helper prints the commits it discards **before** discarding, then resets so
  local `dev` equals `origin/dev`.
- No-op path: when `dev` == `origin/dev` the helper exits 0 with a clear "nothing
  to reconcile" message and mutates nothing.
- `--dry-run` lists and mutates nothing; `--json` emits a machine-readable
  document (commits, owning items, unattributed) stable enough for automation.
- Safety refusals: running in a linked worktree or with `dev` not checked out is
  refused with an actionable message (the helper targets the main checkout).
- Failure safety: a failed push leaves local `dev` unchanged and exits non-zero.

## Minimal implementation

- One hermetic test module driving the script through `subprocess` with a
  sandboxed environment and a local bare remote.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_reconcile_unpushed_dev.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before *Reconcile unpushed dev helper script and docs*.

## Deliverables

- Red-first tests for the reconciliation helper.

# Pre-commit hook refuses main-checkout dev commits

## Goal

As an implement session, I want a commit on `dev` in the main checkout to be
refused at commit time, so a dispatched or ad-hoc agent session can never park a
foreign commit on the shared `dev` ref and block every other session's
`implement.py start`.

Implements parent AC3 (zero-width guard) and the `scripts/install_pi.sh` wiring.

## Context

- `.githooks/` ships `pre-push`, `pre-push.v2`, `post-checkout`, `post-merge`,
  `post-rewrite`, `worklog-post-pull`; `core.hooksPath` is already `.githooks`,
  so a new executable `.githooks/pre-commit` is picked up automatically.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` wires the pre-push hook idempotently (≈319-425) with a
  `# worklog:pre-push-hook:vN` marker comparison and a `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL=1`
  opt-out; the pre-commit hook needs the same treatment.
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` AC1 forbids machine-specific absolute
  paths (`/home/`, `/Users/`, `/root/`) in committed hooks and requires the hook
  to work with a sandboxed `$HOME`.
- A mode-change (`100644 → 100755`) on a tracked file is what gate-refused a
  pre-push during this item's intake — the installed hook must land with a
  deliberate, committed executable bit, not a later chmod.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.githooks/pre-commit` exists, is `#!/bin/sh`, POSIX-only, carries the marker
  `# worklog:pre-commit-hook:v1`, contains no machine-specific absolute path, and
  is committed with mode `100755`.
- Detection: main checkout ⟺ `git rev-parse --git-dir` equals
  `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (a linked worktree's git dir sits under
  `<main>/.git/worktrees/<name>`); target branch ⟺ `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD`
  is `dev`. Both are computed from the hook's own working tree, never a
  hard-coded path.
- Refusal prints one actionable block naming the branch, the checkout path, the
  worktree requirement (`implement.py start`) and the reconciliation helper
  (`scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh`), then exits 1 without mutating anything.
- `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1` proceeds with the commit and prints a loud
  single-line stderr notice so a deliberate operator hot-fix is auditable.
- Silent (exit 0, no output) on every other path: linked worktree, detached
  `HEAD`, feature branch, and any branch other than `dev`.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs/refreshes `pre-commit` beside the pre-push
  wiring, idempotently (marker-compared, never duplicated), honouring
  `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL=1`, and warns loudly instead of failing when the source
  hook is missing.
- The tests from *Pre-commit hook guard sandbox tests* pass, and the pre-commit
  wiring is asserted from the real `install_pi.sh` source (extending
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` or a sibling module).
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` still passes (no machine path, portable
  `sh`).
- Parent AC3 (restated for traceability): A `.githooks/pre-commit` hook refuses a commit on `dev` in the main checkout at commit time (zero-width window — the commit is never created), with an explicit operator override for deliberate hot-fixes, and a `git_sandbox` test proves it fires in the main checkout and does not fire in a worktree or on a feature branch.

## Minimal implementation

- New `.githooks/pre-commit` (~40 lines): detect, decide, exit.
- New wiring block in `scripts/install_pi.sh` modelled on the pre-push block.
- One extension to the installer test module.

## Key Files

- `.githooks/pre-commit` (new)
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` (pre-commit wiring)
- `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py` (from the test item)
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` (extend)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by *Pre-commit hook guard sandbox tests*.

## Deliverables

- The hook, the installer wiring, and green guard/installer tests.

## Goal

As a producer, I want one shared answer to "may this process commit here?", used
by the skill commit helpers AND agreeing with the pre-commit hook, so the audit
skill can never park a remediation commit on `dev` in the main checkout.

and provides the primitive the code-review item consumes.

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_commit_config_remediation` (≈14222)
  commits `ruff` per-file-ignores locally with no push; the call site (≈14439)
  already records failures in `results["chore_failures"]`.
- Detection must equal `.githooks/pre-commit`'s: `--git-dir` == `--git-common-dir`
  and `symbolic-ref --short HEAD` == `dev`, honouring
  `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT`.
- `skill/shared/` is stdlib-only and import-light by convention (see

As a producer, I want **both** `code-review` and `code_review` commit helpers to
refuse a commit on `dev` in the main checkout, so fixing one copy does not leave

## Context

  run `git add .` + `git commit -m "Auto-fix: …"`. They differ in import style

  they are **not** byte-identical twins, and both are imported by live code

# Refactor skill injects finding comments into whatever checkout it runs in

## Problem

Discovered during intake of SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU (downtime workers commit directly
to `dev` in the main checkout).

The refactor skill writes `<!-- REFACTOR-<item-id> -->` markers directly into
source files in its current working directory. When a downtime-dispatched session
runs it with `--cwd <main checkout root>`, it dirties the shared main checkout
without committing anything.

Observed 2026-11-18 ~16:08-16:12 during a concurrent refactor session: the main
checkout was dirtied with `<!-- REFACTOR-SA-… -->` injections in
`scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`,
`skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py`,
`skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py` and
`skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` (plus
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`).

This is a **second main-checkout mutation surface** distinct from the
direct-commit path tracked in SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU: refactor does not commit, but
a dirty checkout `gate-refused` a concurrent pre-push (the same class of damage —
it blocks other sessions' pushes and worktree creation).

## Relation to the parent item

- Parent SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU covers **commits** on `dev` in the main checkout
  (skill commit helpers, the `.githooks/pre-commit` guard, `start` attribution,
  `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh`).
- This item covers **uncommitted writes** by the refactor skill. Its commit-time
  guard does not fire (no commit is made), so it needs its own fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The refactor skill refuses to inject finding comments when its target root is
  the main checkout (detected as `git rev-parse --git-dir` ==
  `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, the same rule as the pre-commit guard), and
  reports an actionable message pointing at the worktree requirement.
- Existing behaviour is preserved in a linked worktree and on a feature branch.
- A `git_sandbox` test pins both the refusal (main checkout unchanged, no
  markers written) and the worktree/feature-branch success path.
- Documentation states that refactor must run in a worktree, cross-referencing
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.

## Impact

A dispatched refactor session can no longer dirty the shared main checkout,
which today blocks concurrent pre-push gates and worktree creation.

## Plan

Decomposed into five child work items, test-first and dependency-ordered:

| # | Work item | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Test: shared is_main_checkout() unit tests | Pin the main-checkout detection rule (`git rev-parse --git-dir` == `--git-common-dir`) |
| 2 | Implement: shared is_main_checkout() helper | One shared predicate in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` next to `main_checkout_root()` |
| 3 | Test: refactor main-checkout refusal and worktree success | `git_sandbox` tests pinning the refusal **and** the preserved worktree/feature-branch path |
| 4 | Implement: refactor main-checkout write refusal | Pipeline pre-flight guard + injection-level defence in depth |
| 5 | Docs: refactor must run in a worktree | `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` plus `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` |

Dependency chain: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 (each implementation item depends on the test
item that pins it).

### Design decisions

- **One detection rule, one implementation.** The guard reuses the
  pre-commit/pre-push rule and is exposed once as
  `git_sandbox.is_main_checkout(path)`; the refactor skill does not re-implement
  git plumbing.
- **Fail fast, before any write.** The guard runs at the start of
  `refactor_pipeline`, before linter auto-fix (ruff/eslint `--fix` also write
  files in place) and before work-item creation. The refusal test can only
  assert "main checkout unchanged" if auto-fix is prevented too.
- **Defence in depth.** `inject_refactor_comment()` also refuses when the target
  file's repository root is the main checkout, so a caller that bypasses the
  pipeline still cannot mark files.
- **`--dry-run` is exempt** — it writes nothing, and read-only inspection of
  the main checkout stays possible.
- **Not in a git work tree → never refuse** (predicate returns `False`), so the
  skill keeps working outside git.
- **Vertical slice note:** effort is Small, so the change is phased as
  test→implementation pairs (shared helper, then refactor behaviour) followed by
  docs; each phase is independently landable and gated by its preceding test
  item. No horizontal layering.

### Effort and risk

Small effort (O=3h, M=6h, P=12h → 6.5h expected, 10.5h with overheads), Medium
risk (7/25; main driver is a false-positive refusal breaking legitimate runs,
mitigated by delegating to the existing git-plumbing rule, exempting
`--dry-run`, and testing the worktree success path).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-18: Initial decomposition (5 children in a test-first dependency
  chain), effort/risk estimated, AC coverage review at 100% (`proceed`).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Seed context: bug item, priority medium, stage `intake_complete` at planning
start, no children, no prior Appendix entries. Discovered during intake of
SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU (downtime workers commit directly to `dev` in the main
checkout); related, non-overlapping items reviewed: SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG
(marker identity, completed), SA-0MVXVBYXI000QMXM and SA-0MVXVC127009T0NP
(pre-push guard failure paths, completed), SA-0MW5KKEHL005BR0L (marker
cross-wiring, open). No existing or completed item covers this refusal.

**Producer interview:** none required — the acceptance criteria already pin the
detection rule, the refusal behaviour, the test requirement and the
documentation requirement. Duplicate-work check performed; no overlapping
completed item found.

**OPEN QUESTION (to: producer, non-blocking)** — AC2 reads "Existing behaviour
is preserved in a linked worktree and on a feature branch." Under the stated
detection rule, a feature branch checked out **in the main checkout** is still
the main checkout (`git-dir` == `git-common-dir`) and would therefore be
refused. The plan assumes "feature branch" means the normal agent flow — a
feature branch inside a linked worktree created by `implement.py start` — and
preserves that path. Why it matters: the alternative reading (allow the main
checkout when the branch is not `dev`) needs a different detection rule than
the one AC1 prescribes. Assumption adopted; nothing is blocked.

**Decision (agent, from the item text)** — the refusal is fail-fast at pipeline
start rather than a per-injection skip, because AC3 requires the refusal test to
assert "main checkout unchanged", which is only true when auto-fix writes are
prevented as well as marker injection.

**Decision (agent)** — the predicate lives in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`
beside `main_checkout_root()`/`is_worktree_git_dir()` so the commit-helper
guard items (SA-0MWMCVFXB0096UG5, SA-0MWMCVNK0003QVW8) reuse one rule instead
of growing a third copy.

**Observed at planning time (evidence, not a work item)** — the main checkout
was dirty with exactly the described artefacts (`scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`,
`skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`,
`skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py`,
`skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py`,
`skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py`,
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`), a live reproduction by a concurrent
dispatched refactor session. The planning session made no changes to those
files.
data.title: Refactor skill injects finding comments into the main checkout
